title: UK Home Office tells blind Nigerian pensioner to go home to India
content: A 67‑year‑old blind Nigerian pensioner named Comfort, who arrived in the United Kingdom in 2000, was refused indefinite leave to remain under the Home Office’s new settlement rules. The Home Office told her she can safely “go home” to India. Comfort became blind shortly after arriving, when she developed acute glaucoma. The decision reflects the Home Office’s assessment of her immigration status despite her 26 years of residence in the UK.
summary: A 67‑year‑old blind Nigerian pensioner who has lived in the UK for 26 years was refused indefinite leave to remain under the Home Office’s new settlement rules. The Home Office told her she can safely “go home” to India.

title: Bristol targets UK’s first wetland city status with 5‑year flood‑risk project
content: Five-year project will create wildlife corridors by building wetlands and increase access to green and blue spaces Bristol could become home to the UK’s first “wetland city” thanks to a charity’s efforts to create vast wildlife corridors that will reduce flood risk and give people more access to green and blue spaces. The Wildfowl & Wetlands Trust (WWT) said the five-year initiative would include more than 200 projects to restore and create wetlands across the city. These will range from small household rainwater ponds and street-level rain gardens to restoring river habitats, reconnecting rivers with their floodplains, and creating new wetlands.
summary: The Wildfowl & Wetlands Trust announced a five‑year initiative to create over 200 wetlands and wildlife corridors across Bristol. The projects will include household rainwater ponds, street‑level rain gardens, river habitat restoration, floodplain reconnection and new wetland creation to reduce flood risk and expand green and blue space access.

content:
Artists and industry figures are urging the culture secretary to outlaw ticket resale for profit, calling for a shutdown of touts. A ticket reseller is advertising £1 million worth of tickets for U2’s 2027 “The Greatest Show on Earth” tour on StubHub, prompting scrutiny of the platform’s stance against professional traders who use “bot” software to acquire tickets and resell them.

Seats for the four‑night London leg of the tour sold out last week, shortly after the tickets went on sale. The large resale listing has raised questions about StubHub’s condemnation of such bot‑driven resale practices.
summary: A tout is advertising £1 million of tickets for U2’s 2027 “The Greatest Show on Earth” tour on StubHub. The four‑night London leg sold out last week, leading artists and industry figures to urge the culture secretary to ban resale for profit and prompting questions about StubHub’s stance on bot‑used ticket traders.

title: Hundreds of English children under 12 prescribed GLP‑1 weight‑loss drugs
content:
An investigation revealed that hundreds of children in England are being prescribed GLP‑1 medications, with some recipients younger than 12, according to figures disclosed by the Guardian. Experts highlighted the importance of specialist supervision and long‑term monitoring for these young patients.  

GLP‑1 drugs were originally developed to help people with type 2 diabetes manage blood‑sugar levels, but they have also become widely used as weight‑loss treatments, with products such as Wegovy and Mounjaro noted as household names.
summary: An investigation found that hundreds of children in England, including some under 12, have been prescribed GLP‑1 medications. Experts say these weight‑loss drugs, originally for type 2 diabetes, require specialist supervision and long‑term monitoring.

title: Central European University plans to expand programmes in Budapest, says interim rector
content: Central European University, which was forced to leave Hungary under Viktor Orbán, is now reaching out to the new government and signalling confidence in the country’s democratic future. Interim president and rector Carsten Q Schneider said the university is interested in expanding its programmes in Budapest, provided the move does not compromise the student experience. The prospect of a partial return to the capital reflects CEU’s willingness to broaden its presence in Hungary while monitoring the impact on its academic community.
summary: The Central European University, which Viktor Orbán tried to chase out of Hungary, is open to expanding its presence in Budapest. Interim president and rector Carsten Q Schneider said the university wants to increase programmes there provided it does not damage the student experience.

title: EU approves airport‑style passport and fingerprint checks at Eurotunnel to curb border chaos
content:
Getlink, the owner of Eurotunnel, has announced plans to replicate an “airport experience” at the Folkestone and Calais terminals, allowing travellers to remain in their vehicles while undergoing passport and fingerprinting checks. The new controls aim to prevent both short‑term and long‑term chaos in the two border towns.

In a breakthrough for travellers, the European Commission has approved the use of an “eagle eye” camera system—already employed at Rome and Paris airports to supervise fingerprinting and facial imaging—at the UK‑France border.
summary: Getlink wants to introduce airport‑style passport and fingerprint controls at the Eurotunnel to keep travelers in their cars and avoid chaos in Folkestone and Calais. The European Commission has agreed to use an “eagle eye” camera system, similar to those in Rome and Paris airports, for fingerprinting and facial imaging at the UK‑France border.

content:
Sydney and Melbourne airports reported that US‑bound flights were grounded or delayed on Saturday after American authorities halted departures and delayed landings at all US airports. The disruption followed a telecommunications outage that prompted a temporary ban on departures, which has now been lifted.

At Melbourne, passengers scheduled to leave for Los Angeles shortly after 10 a.m. faced a delay of almost three hours. Similar impacts were noted at Sydney, where several flights were also affected by the halt.

title: Astronaut Suni Williams rides through NYC as Grand Marshal of the Veterans Day Parade | Space photo of the day for Nov. 13, 2026
content: NASA astronaut Suni Williams rides through New York City as the Grand Marshal of the Veterans Day Parade on Nov. 11, 2026. (Image credit: Photo by Slaven Vlasic/Getty Images) New Yorkers got a space-y surprise on Wednesday (Nov. 11): Retired NASA astronaut and U. S. Navy Captain Sunita "Suni" Williams rolled down 5th Avenue in the back of a classic convertible wrapped in patriotic decals as Grand Marshal of the Veterans Day Parade. What is it? On Wednesday, New York City's 107th annual Veterans Day Parade made its way through Manhattan to the cheers and respectful nods of thousands of onlookers. The parade is an annual tradition on the holiday, which honors veterans of the U. S. Armed forces. As part of the parade, veterans, active-duty soldiers, firefighters, marching bands, youth cadets and more march through the city and honor those who have served and sacrificed in the U. S. Military. This year, the parade featured Suni Williams as its grand marshal. "I’m proud to join New Yorkers and Americans from around the country in honoring the service, sacrifice, and commitment of veterans from every generation," she said during the event. Why is it incredible? Williams was selected for NASA's astronaut program in 1998 and retired from it in December 2025. She spent 608 days in space during her astronaut career, the second-most by an American astronaut behind Peggy Whitson, who racked up 695. Williams also had an extensive career in the U. S. Navy. She began as an ensign in 1987 before serving in a number of different roles. For example, she was a diving officer and a naval aviator and also provided helicopter combat support during Operation Desert Shield and Operation Provide Comfort. She further served as a squadron safety officer and finally as a captain, a rank she achieved in 2017. During this time, Williams supported relief efforts following Hurricane Andrew, trained within the U. S. Naval Test Pilot School and gained a wealth of further experience flying as a military pilot. Williams is part of a longstanding tradition of astronauts serving in the U. S. Military. From test pilots to naval officers and more, there's a strong link between the U. S. Armed forces and NASA's astronaut program.
summary: NASA astronaut Suni Williams rides through New York City as the Grand Marshal of the Veterans Day Parade on Nov. 11, 2026.

title: Mariner 9 becomes first spacecraft to orbit Mars on Nov. 13, 1971
content:
On November 13, 1971, NASA’s Mariner 9 became the first spacecraft to enter orbit around Mars. At the time of the launch, scientists had only limited knowledge of the Red Planet. Earlier Mars fly‑bys had revealed a cratered surface, leading some to think Mars resembled the Moon. Mariner 9 changed that perception when it arrived in the middle of a global dust storm. The probe’s cameras captured tall structures that, once the dust settled, were identified as the tops of huge volcanoes. Among them was Olympus Mons, the tallest volcano in the solar system.

The mission also revealed Valles Marineris, an enormous canyon five times longer than the Grand Canyon in Arizona. Mariner 9 mapped 85 % of the planet’s surface during its nearly one‑year orbit. It carried four primary instruments—a camera system, an ultraviolet spectrometer, an infrared spectrometer, and an infrared radiometer—that enabled the discovery of 20 giant volcanoes and detailed mapping of Valles Marineris, which stretches 2,500 miles (4,000 km) long and 120 miles (200 km) wide. The canyon was named in honor of the spacecraft.

In total, Mariner 9 took 7,329 photographs of Mars, achieving a resolution of between ½ and 1 mile (1–2 km). It also captured at least 80 images of Mars’ two small moons, Phobos and Deimos. The probe’s gaseous nitrogen supply, used to feed its attitude‑control thrusters, ran dry by February 1972. NASA shut the mission down in October 1972 after the spacecraft had completed its orbit.

Mariner 9’s achievements cemented its place in space history. It was the first human‑made object to orbit Mars, beating the Soviet Union’s Mars 2 spacecraft to the planet despite Mars 2’s 11‑day head start. The data gathered by Mariner 9 transformed the image of Mars from a mysterious, moon‑like world into a fully mapped planet, laying the groundwork for future exploration.
summary: On Nov. 13, 1971, NASA's Mariner 9 entered orbit around Mars, the first human‑built craft to do so. The mission mapped about 85% of the planet, revealing features such as Olympus Mons and the Valles Marineris canyon.

content:

Kiss identified Gordon as the playmaker intended to stabilize the No 10 position, a role that has seen seven different starting flyhalves since the last World Cup. The team is aiming to avoid a fourth consecutive loss following their recent defeat to England.

In other squad changes, Meredith was dropped from the match-day 23 after the loss to England, while Valetini was named in the starting XV. Kiss expressed confidence that Gordon and Valetini will be the difference makers as the team attempts to improve its performance in Edinburgh.

title: Ponga and Walsh lead Australia and New Zealand into Rugby League World Cup final
content:
The Rugby League World Cup men’s final in Brisbane will feature a rematch between Australia and New Zealand, marking their first meeting in the tournament’s decider since 2013. The article notes that this encounter follows previous finals where England failed to defeat Australia in 2017 and Samoa lost to the Kangaroos four years prior. Full-backs Ponga and Walsh are highlighted as taking center stage in this matchup between old rivals.

The tournament has seen significant changes, including new formats, the rise of new nations, and a rare financial profit. Despite this evolution, the final brings a familiar dynamic to the competition. Following the men’s final in Brisbane, Australia and New Zealand are set to meet again in the women’s decider.
summary: Full-backs Ponga and Walsh take centre stage as Australia and New Zealand meet in the men's final in Brisbane. This is the first time the two rivals have contested the final since 2013, following previous losses by England and Samoa.

title: McCullum backs Pietersen to help England after Perth ODI collapse
content:
Brendon McCullum has supported Kevin Pietersen’s role in educating England’s batting lineup, a position the “specialist mentor” will hold until the tour of Australia concludes after Sunday’s second one-day international in Adelaide. This endorsement follows England’s dismissal for 131 in the opening ODI in Perth, which resulted in a seven-wicket defeat. McCullum indicated that Pietersen’s message to the team would be measured but firm.

The low total evoked memories of the first Ashes Test from a year prior, though the current situation is considered more relevant for future challenges. Specifically, the performance highlights concerns about encountering similarly fast, bouncy surfaces, such as the Wanderers in Johannesburg, during next year’s 50-over World Cup in southern Africa.
summary: Brendon McCullum supports Kevin Pietersen in educating England's batting lineup following a 131 all-out defeat in Perth. The collapse on a bouncy pitch raised concerns about similar conditions at the upcoming 50-over World Cup in southern Africa.

title: John McGinn double saves Scotland from North Macedonia defeat
content:
John McGinn scored twice, including a penalty, to secure a victory for Scotland against North Macedonia. The match was described as a significant struggle for the home side, who faced a team that threatened to cause a major upset. While the result preserved Scotland’s honor, the performance raised questions about manager Sébastien Pocognoli’s ability to build on the work of his predecessor, Steve Clarke.

The occasion also marked a milestone for Andy Robertson, who earned his 102nd cap. This achievement places him level with Kenny Dalglish on the all-time Scottish list, positioning him to become the record holder soon. Despite this individual landmark, the article notes that Pocognoli appeared tactically inflexible, suggesting the team is currently a difficult watch rather than entering the new era many had predicted.
summary: John McGinn scored twice, including a penalty, to secure a draw for Scotland against North Macedonia. Andy Robertson also reached his 102nd cap, tying Kenny Dalglish for the most in Scottish history.

content: Researchers at Vilnius University report that whole-blood NAD levels remain stable with age in healthy men and increase slightly in women. However, the study of more than 1,000 adults found that these levels are lower in individuals with cardiovascular disease, particularly those with hypertension.
summary: Vilnius University researchers found that whole-blood NAD levels remain stable with age in healthy men. The levels increase slightly in women and are lower in people with cardiovascular disease, especially hypertension.

title: Scientists say scent‑memory link is complex and evidence for aromatherapy benefits is mixed
content: The sense of smell is closely linked to memory, prompting vivid recollections when a scent associated with a past experience is encountered. This relationship has sparked claims that aromatherapy may improve memory or reduce cognitive decline. However, researchers are still working to understand how the brain connects scent to experience, and scientific studies to date provide mixed evidence for those memory‑enhancing claims.
summary: The sense of smell is closely linked to memory, and odors associated with past events can trigger vivid recollections. However, researchers say brain mechanisms are still being unraveled and scientific evidence for aromatherapy’s memory benefits is mixed.

title: SpaceX Starship launches for double catch attempt
content:
SpaceX’s Starship megarocket, the world’s largest rocket at 407 ft tall, launched from Starbase in south Texas on Friday afternoon. The company aimed to make history with a double catch of the reusable vehicle.

Flight 15 is expected to orbit Earth about 14 times over a 22‑hour period. After completing its circuit, SpaceX plans to recover the rocket at its launchpad at Starbase.

The mission’s goal is to demonstrate the feasibility of reusing the Starship by catching it after a full orbital run.

title: FAA Issues Nationwide Ground Stop, Halting Flights Across US
content:
The Federal Aviation Administration issued a nationwide ground stop on Friday, halting takeoffs across the United States. The order was announced “due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety,” but aircraft already airborne were permitted to land.

In a tweet sent shortly after 5 p.m. Eastern Time, the FAA explained that a temporary telecommunications outage prompted the precautionary halt. The agency confirmed that every flight had been accounted for and that international flights would be managed on a case‑by‑case basis. At 6:16 p.m. ET, FlightAware reported 10,494 U.S. flights delayed and 3,396 flights canceled.

A photo accompanying the report shows Delta Air Lines planes parked at LaGuardia Airport on June 3, 2026, illustrating the widespread impact of the ground stop.
summary: The FAA issued a national ground stop on Friday, halting all flights in the US due to a temporary telecommunications outage. FlightAware reports 10,494 flights delayed and 3,396 canceled as of 6:16PM ET, while planes in the air are allowed to land.

title: Amazon Plans to Index Global Online Shopping Data with World Product Graph
content:
Amazon is preparing a data‑vault that would catalog every product sold on the internet, including items the retailer itself does not offer, Reuters reports. The initiative, named the “World Product Graph,” will make the compiled information accessible through Amazon’s own website.

According to the report, the project aims to keep shoppers from turning to platforms such as Reddit or Google for product research and to increase the likelihood that they purchase through Amazon, even when searching for items sold elsewhere. The plan also envisions that AI agents might preferentially use Amazon’s extensive product index when assisting shoppers.
summary: Amazon Plans to Index Global Online Shopping Data with World Product Graph.

title: OpenAI board member warns AI takeover could happen within months
content: How do you think you're going to die? If you go by the current statistics for deaths in the US, it's reasonable to expect that cancer or heart disease will eventually get you. But OpenAI Foundation board member and Alignment Research Center Executive Director Paul Cristiano thinks we should all be worried about another major mortality risk. Speaking at a lecture series this week, Cristiano bluntly told the audience in a Toronto Convention Center, "I think for most people in this room, the most likely reason they will die is because of an AI accident." In the opening lecture of a three-part series, Cristiano outlined his worries about the risk of an impending "AI takeover." He defined that as a situation where goal-pursuing AI systems "call the shots in the same sense that humans today call the shots and what happens on Earth" and where any human trying to stop them "would be as ineffective as if you or me was trying to stop the US military." Such a situation would likely lead to mass death and perhaps uninhabitable environments for humans, Cristiano said. Read full article Comments
summary: How do you think you're going to die? If you go by the current statistics for deaths in the US, it's reasonable to expect that cancer or heart disease will eventually get you.

title: Millions of Americans are not taking their GLP-1 drugs as prescribed
content:
GLP‑1 medications have become widely used for diabetes, weight loss, and several other chronic conditions, including cardiovascular disease and obstructive sleep apnea. A new study from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) shows that the drugs are also being used in ways that diverge from medical prescriptions.

The CDC researchers analyzed survey data collected in July and August 2025 from more than 8,000 U.S. adults. Their estimates indicate that about 9.8 percent of U.S. adults—roughly 27 million people—used a glucagon‑like peptide‑1 receptor agonist in 2025. The study was published in the CDC’s Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report.

Among those who reported using a GLP‑1 drug, 44 percent said they altered their use from the prescribed regimen. Reported changes included skipping doses, delaying refills, and taking smaller doses, among other modifications.

More than half of the users who changed their usage cited cost or availability as the reason for doing so. Cost and access barriers were most pronounced among younger adults: 58 percent of users aged 14‑39 who modified their use named cost as a barrier, compared with only 20 percent of users aged 65 or older who reported the same.
summary: GLP-1 medications are everywhere these days. The peptide-based drugs are both highly effective and wildly popular for diabetes, weight loss and a growing range of connected chronic health conditions, including cardiovascular disease and obstructive sleep apnea.
author: Ars Technica

title: FAA Issues Third Nationwide Ground Stop Over Telecommunications Outage
content:
The Federal Aviation Administration issued its third nationwide ground stop, halting all departures from U.S. airports on Friday afternoon. The order came days after the agency expanded the use of an artificial‑intelligence tool.

Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy announced the ground stop on X, explaining that a “communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers” had prompted the decision. He said FAA staff were troubleshooting the problem and would provide updates as more information became available.

Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin clarified that the stop was not triggered by a security threat. He described it as a telecommunications outage within the FAA and noted that the agency would handle incoming international flights on a case‑by‑case basis, adding that there was no indication of a nefarious attack.
summary: The FAA issued a nationwide ground stop, halting departures from all US airports, after a telecommunications outage affecting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers. Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy announced the stop on X, and DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin said the issue was not a security threat and that international flights would be handled case‑by‑case.

title: Starship Flight 15 Reaches Orbit, Prepares for Saturday Catch
content:
Starship flight 15 lifted off on schedule from Starbase, Texas, on Friday, marking the spacecraft’s 15th test flight in more than three years. The launch occurred in the early evening, with the Sun setting over the western horizon as the massive rocket ascended. Atmospheric winds were calm, allowing the rocket’s white plume to remain visible for several minutes.

The first stage of the vehicle climbed toward space without issue, releasing the upper stage over the Gulf of Mexico. The Starship upper stage then ignited its Raptor engines and entered a nominal low‑Earth orbit. This flight represents the second time SpaceX has successfully placed a Starship vehicle into orbit.
summary: Starship lifted off from Starbase, Texas on Friday, completing its 15th test flight. The upper stage ignited Raptor engines and entered a nominal low‑Earth orbit, marking SpaceX's second successful orbit of the vehicle.
author: Ars Technica

title: FAA Issues Nationwide Ground Stop Over Communication Issues at Air Route Centers

title: Report revisits Afghanistan's Ring Road after US war and five years of Taliban rule
content:
Highway 1, also known as the Ring Road, links Afghanistan’s major cities and has long been a vital transport corridor. After the September 11, 2001 attacks, the route turned into a hotspot for crime and fighting, especially between Kabul and Kandahar, the Taliban’s birthplace, with travelers facing extortions, kidnappings and suicide bombings.  

To assess the road’s condition following the US‑led war and five years of Taliban rule, former Afghanistan correspondent Claire Billet and photojournalist Sandra Calligaro returned to the country to investigate.
summary: Highway 1, or the Ring Road, connects Afghanistan's major cities. After September 11, 2001, it became a hotspot for crime and fighting, particularly between the capital Kabul and Kandahar, the Taliban's birthplace.

title: California's brand-new Air & Space Center, home of the space shuttle Endeavour, opens today
content:
The California Science Center in Los Angeles officially opened its new Samuel Oschin Air & Space Center to the public on November 13. This massive new wing, which has been in development for more than three decades, centers on the retired space shuttle Endeavour. The spacecraft is displayed upright in its launch position, standing nearly 200 feet tall. Former NASA astronaut Garrett Reisman, who flew on two space shuttle missions including one on Endeavour, described the initial reveal of the shuttle as an overwhelming experience. He noted that the exhibit provides a significant opportunity for people from around the world to visit Los Angeles and see the shuttle, creating a "force multiplier" for exposing children and families to space exploration.

Visitors enter the exhibit through a video presentation that culminates in a dramatic unveiling of the shuttle, which completed 25 missions to Earth orbit between 1992 and 2011. The display features a replica launch tower that allows guests to look down at the spacecraft. At the base of the shuttle, there are numerous interactive exhibits, including a shuttle landing simulator, a replica cockpit, and various space artifacts from decades of spaceflight history. While visitors can use elevators or stairs to navigate the space, they can also slide down to the base of the exhibit.

The interior of the shuttle is open for inspection, allowing visitors to peer inside at the robotic arm, handles, straps, and electronic gear. The exhibit is designed for all ages and offers multiple vantage points, including a view from underneath the engines and a transparent floor at the top of the launch tower that allows visitors to stand above the shuttle. Reisman reflected on his time aboard the shuttle, pointing out specific handrails he held during a spacewalk. He explained that seeing these same handrails from the elevator triggers memories of his training and mission, emphasizing the direct connection between the historical artifact and the public experience.

The new air and space center is free to the public, just like the rest of the museum. However, due to the high anticipation surrounding the opening, visitors are required to make online reservations to attend. While the admission is free, there is a cost associated with reserving slots during the busy initial days. The California Science Center encourages visitors to budget a significant amount of time to explore the full range of exhibits and interactive elements available in the new wing.
summary: California's brand-new Air & Space Center, home of the space shuttle Endeavour, opens today.
author: Space.com

title: Rocket Lab launching 100th space mission early on Nov. 14: Watch it live
content:
Rocket Lab is scheduled to launch its 100th space mission, designated "The Mountain God Rises," early Saturday morning, November 14. The Electron rocket, carrying a private Japanese Earth-observing satellite, will lift off from the company’s New Zealand site during a window opening at 12:30 a.m. EST (0530 GMT; 6:30 p.m. local time). Live coverage will begin approximately 30 minutes before launch and is available via Rocket Lab, with Space.com expected to carry the feed.

This milestone marks the 100th launch for the California-based company since its first test flight in May 2017. Although that initial effort failed, the 59-foot-tall Electron rocket successfully delivered cubesats to low Earth orbit in January 2018. Rocket Lab founder and CEO Peter Beck stated during a November 9 earnings call that no commercially developed rocket has reached the 100-launch mark faster, including SpaceX’s Falcon 9. Beck highlighted that the company has achieved a 96% reliability rate across its previous 99 launches, describing the achievement as an unprecedented milestone for a commercial small-lift orbital rocket.

For this specific mission, the Electron rocket features special black livery to commemorate the golden milestone. The launch will be the 11th for Tokyo-based customer iQPS, which is developing a constellation of 36 synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellites. If successful, the rocket’s upper kick stage will deploy a single iQPS spacecraft into an orbit 357 miles (575 kilometers) above Earth. These SAR satellites are capable of imaging the planet through cloud cover and at night, providing advantages over optical-wavelength spacecraft. It is noted that not all of Rocket Lab’s missions are orbital; its suborbital HASTE variant has conducted nine missions to date.
summary: Rocket Lab will launch its 100th space mission early Saturday morning (Nov. 14), and you can watch the milestone liftoff live.
author: Space.com

title: Jonbon wins Shloer Chase at Cheltenham despite ground issues
content:
Jonbon extended his remarkable career record on Friday by winning the Shloer Chase at Cheltenham for the third time in the last four seasons. The popular chaser maintained his lifetime streak of never finishing outside the first two in 29 starts under National Hunt rules. However, the victory felt somewhat flat, a sentiment attributed to several negative factors affecting the day, including ground issues, horses slipping, and the low sun.

The race took place on the opening day of Cheltenham’s second-biggest meeting, which proved to be a trying day for the venue. Jonbon was left with only two rivals to beat after Gidleigh Park, the second-favourite on Friday morning, was ruled out a couple of hours before the start. This withdrawal was due to concerns about the drying ground, highlighting the challenging conditions present at the troubled home of jumps racing.
summary: Jonbon won the Shloer Chase for the third time in four seasons to extend his streak of finishing in the first two in 29 National Hunt starts. The race was affected by drying ground and low sun, which led to the second-favorite Gidleigh Park being withdrawn before the start.

It was only a matter of when. Pochettino is famously emotional, and nobody in attendance had to wait long for the waterworks – they came during his introductory remarks, as he thanked the US Soccer executives flanking him for the opportunity to guide the US men. He grew emotional again as he addressed his impending departure for Manchester United, one announced just hours earlier. “I think [the decision was],” Pochettino said, pausing to compose himself, “one of the most difficult decisions of our careers. Thank you guys. Thank you so much.”

content: Democrats are preparing to retake the majority in both the House and Senate, asserting they hold a mandate to deliver change. However, internal divisions have emerged regarding who should lead the party.

title: Burnham pledges new era of British climate leadership at Cop summit
content:
Jonathan Freedland, a Guardian columnist, argues that Andy Burnham faces a significant challenge in balancing climate action with economic growth. Freedland notes that while activists contend that addressing the climate crisis is economically sound, politicians must manage immediate voter demands for affordability and growth. Burnham, who addressed the Cop summit in Antalya, promised “a new era of British leadership” in the fight against global heating.

According to Freedland, Burnham’s political strategy involves reducing the appeal of the Green Party, whose electoral success earlier in the year contributed to the departure of his predecessor. The columnist emphasizes that while rhetorical commitments are important, they must ultimately be followed by concrete actions to resolve the dilemma between environmental imperatives and economic expectations.
summary: Andy Burnham addressed the Cop summit in Antalya, promising a new era of British leadership in the struggle against global heating. His political strategy relies on shrinking the appeal of the Green party, whose electoral success helped remove his predecessor.
author: Guardian Environment

title: The Guardian view on M John Harrison’s Booker win: a new frontier for science fiction | Editorial
content: The End of Everything is a novel for our age of permacrisis. Genre boundaries belong to the past “Science fiction will never be Literature with a capital ‘L,’” began a New York Times review of Margaret Atwood’s novel Oryx and Crake back in 2003. Now, the seemingly impossible has happened – M John Harrison’s The End of Everything is the first science fiction novel to win the Booker prize. Fans have hailed this as a victory for a long-marginalised genre. The author himself was not so sure. “Writing science fiction is the last thing I want to do,” he said with characteristic iconoclasm at an event before the prize. The sci-fi v literary or “mainstream” fiction debate is as endless and battle-strewn as a fantasy saga. The late Ursula K Le Guin, a giant of the form, famously took Atwood to task for her reluctance to use the term science fiction for some of her novels, including Oryx and Crake: “She doesn’t want the literary bigots to shove her into the literary ghetto.” Harrison doesn’t want to break out of the ghetto; he wants to break it down. “I really hate categories, and I really hate being categorised,” he said.
summary: The End of Everything is a novel for our age of permacrisis. Genre boundaries belong to the past “Science fiction will never be Literature with a capital ‘L,’” began a New York Times review of Margaret Atwood’s novel Oryx and Crake back in 2003.
author: Guardian Environment

title: California Governor Gavin Newsom Endorses Global Fossil Fuel Phaseout
content:
California Governor Gavin Newsom, the most prominent US politician attending Cop31, has explicitly endorsed a global phaseout of fossil fuels. Speaking to the Guardian, Newsom stated that California is “100%” behind the Santa Marta coalition, a group of over 50 countries including many of the world’s largest economies. The coalition aims to transition away from oil, gas, and coal toward solar, wind, batteries, and other non-carbon energy sources.

Newsom’s participation highlights a significant diplomatic presence for the United States, as the Trump administration continues to boycott the climate process. As the leader of the world’s fourth-largest economy, Newsom’s endorsement underscores California’s commitment to aligning with international efforts to address climate breakdown through a shift to cleaner energy systems.
summary: California Governor Gavin Newsom stated that California is 100% behind the Santa Marta coalition's efforts to transition away from oil, gas, and coal. He is the most prominent US politician at Cop31, a process the Trump administration continues to boycott.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Study links PFOS to early development issues in stem cell model
content: A study from Karolinska Institutet, published in Human Reproduction Open, indicates that PFOS, a persistent PFAS substance, can interfere with critical early germ cell and embryonic development processes. These findings are based on research utilizing stem cell-derived models of early human development.
summary: Research from Karolinska Institutet indicates that PFOS can interfere with processes critical for early germ cell and embryonic development. The study, which utilized stem cell-derived models, is published in the journal Human Reproduction Open.

title: Longer inhibitory connections push simulated neural networks beyond critical tipping point
content: The brain criticality hypothesis in neuroscience suggests that neurons are organized so that neural activity exists near a transition point between two distinct states. This critical point separates an ordered, subcritical state, where activity dissipates rapidly, from a disordered, supercritical state, where activity spreads quickly and may grow uncontrollably. The provided text outlines these fundamental definitions to establish the framework for understanding neural network dynamics.
summary: Longer inhibitory connections push simulated neural networks beyond the critical tipping point. This shift moves the network from a subcritical to a supercritical regime, altering the spread of neural activity.

title: Rutgers Health finds gut bacteria molecule that may reverse gut damage via NAD
content: Scientists at Rutgers Health have identified a molecule produced by “good” gut bacteria that rapidly heals the intestinal lining. The compound protects against severe inflammatory diseases and stimulates the production of a coenzyme whose levels normally decline with age.
summary: Scientists at Rutgers Health have discovered a molecule produced by good gut bacteria that rapidly heals the intestinal lining and protects against severe inflammatory diseases. The molecule also triggers increased production of NAD, a coenzyme whose levels diminish with age.
author: Medical Xpress

title: New mouse brain map traces origins of complex multi-part movements
content: A new biological blueprint mapping how a mouse’s body is represented in its brain has been published in Nature Communications. This research aims to help scientists address a fundamental question regarding the coordination of complex motions that involve multiple body parts, such as using the arm, hand, head, and lips to sip soup.
summary: A new biological blueprint shows how a mouse's body is represented in its brain. The study was published in Nature Communications.

title: Study: Compounded GLP-1s dominate weight-loss market with untested additives
content: A new study reveals that compounded GLP-1 receptor agonist medications now constitute a large majority of weight-loss medicines. These products combine GLP-1s with other active substances, some of which are not regulated by the FDA. The research highlights that these compounded formulations frequently include vitamin B12 analogs that have not been tested for safety in combination with GLP-1s. This finding comes as the use of GLP-1 medications has skyrocketed in recent years, with many individuals opting for these compounded versions.
summary: A new study found that compounded GLP-1 products now make up a large majority of weight-loss medicines. These products commonly contain vitamin B12 analogs that have not been tested for safety in combination with GLP-1s.

title: Tübingen and Calgary researchers identify gut bacteria driving inflammatory bowel disease
content:
An international research team led by Dr. Lukas Mager of University Hospital Tübingen and Prof. Kathy McCoy of the University of Calgary has developed a method to identify and selectively target gut bacteria that contribute to chronic inflammation. The researchers identified two specific bacterial species that promote intestinal inflammation and discovered compounds capable of selectively inhibiting their growth.

Published in the journal Gut, this study could pave the way for personalized therapies for inflammatory bowel diseases (IBD), including Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis.

content: Bioengineers at the University of California San Diego have developed a technology enabling drugs to regulate the timing of therapeutic protein production in cells. This innovation could potentially enhance the safety and adaptability of gene therapies for the treatment of chronic diseases.
summary: Bioengineers at the University of California San Diego developed a technology that allows drugs to control when cells produce therapeutic proteins. This innovation could potentially make gene therapies safer and more adaptable for treating chronic diseases.

title: IEA: Global oil supply returns to surplus for first time since Iran war
content:
The International Energy Agency (IEA) reported that global oil supply returned to a surplus in October, marking the first such shift since the start of the US-Israeli war against Iran. According to the Paris-based agency, oil supplies exceeded demand by nearly two million barrels per day during the month.

The IEA attributed this rebalancing to Gulf exports recovering much faster than global oil demand. The agency described the market as showing “tentative signs of rebalancing” as supply levels outstripped consumption.
summary: The International Energy Agency stated that global oil supplies exceeded demand by almost 2 million barrels a day in October. This marks the first surplus since the start of the US-Israeli war against Iran, driven by Gulf exports recovering faster than global demand.

title: Ancient granitic rocks on Türkiye's Marmara Sea reveal deep Earth origins
content: Granitic rocks exposed along the southern shores and islands of Türkiye's Marmara Sea originated as molten material deep within Earth's crust. These surface rocks preserve records of regions they occupied millions of years ago, even when those areas were located kilometers below ground.
summary: Surface rocks can reveal records of regions they occupied millions of years ago, even if those areas were kilometers below ground. Granitic rocks now exposed on Türkiye's Marmara Sea's southern shores and islands originated as molten material deep in Earth's crust.

content: A new genetic atlas reveals traces of 10,000 years of selective sheep breeding. Humans have consistently chosen animals for desirable traits, including wool, size, and reproductive characteristics, which has gradually left a mark on their DNA.
summary: For around 10,000 years, humans have selectively bred sheep for desirable traits. Generation after generation, we have chosen animals for their wool, size and reproductive characteristics and gradually left our mark on their DNA.

content: Mercury contamination is difficult to detect because it is invisible to the naked eye, allowing toxic trace amounts to remain hidden in items like water or fruit. Currently, identifying these minute levels typically necessitates the use of specialized laboratory equipment and expertise from trained professionals.
summary: Mercury contamination presents an obvious challenge: it is invisible. A glass of water or a piece of fruit can seem perfectly normal to the naked eye, even when trace amounts of toxic mercury are present.

content: Nyana rooiwalensis, a newly identified dinosaur species from South Africa, lived over 200 million years ago. This bipedal animal weighed approximately 400 kilograms (880 pounds) while still a youngster, making it a heavyweight even in its youth.
summary: The newly identified dinosaur species Nyana rooiwalensis lived in South Africa more than 200 million years ago. It likely walked on two legs and weighed about 400 kilograms despite still being a young individual.

title: Chromium keeps ruthenium grounded in water electrolysis
content:
Researchers at ICFO are investigating ruthenium as a single‑atom catalyst for water electrolysis, a process that splits water to produce green hydrogen. The metal’s high activity makes it attractive for accelerating the reaction.  

However, during operation ruthenium tends to over‑oxidize and dissolve, which can limit its practical use. The study suggests that chromium can keep ruthenium grounded, helping to stabilize the catalyst and prevent its loss.
summary: Chromium keeps ruthenium grounded in water electrolysis. Ruthenium, used in single-atom catalysts for water electrolysis, tends to over-oxidize and dissolve during operation.

content: Recent research indicates that dogs, which have lived with humans for tens of thousands of years, are highly attuned to human emotions. Behavioral experiments, brain imaging, and heart‑rate measurements all show that dogs respond differently to varying emotional expressions in humans.
summary: Dogs have lived with humans for tens of thousands of years and are highly attuned to human emotions. Behavioral experiments, brain studies and heart‑rate measurements show that dogs respond differently to varying emotional expressions.

title: Gemini Astronaut Photos Inspired Early Earth Observation Program
content:
NASA astronauts James A. Lovell Jr. and Edwin E. “Buzz” Aldrin Jr. captured images of the Red Sea and Nile river valley on November 14, 1966, during their four-day mission aboard Gemini XII. This flight, which ran from November 11 to 15, marked the final mission of NASA’s Gemini program. While the crew successfully completed rendezvous maneuvers and spacewalks, procedures essential for future Moon missions, they also contributed to the development of Earth observation from space.

The orbital imagery captured by Lovell, Aldrin, and other Gemini astronauts demonstrated the value of such photography for studying Earth’s surface. These images helped scientists build a case for a dedicated Earth observation satellite program. William T. Pecora, the director of the United States Geological Survey from 1965 to 1971, was a key advocate for accelerating the use of these satellites. In a 1969 statement, Pecora noted that the Earth Resources Observation Satellite (EROS) program, which he championed, was conceived in 1966 largely as a direct result of the demonstrated utility of Mercury and Gemini orbital photography for Earth resource studies.

The EROS program later paved the way for Landsat, which has provided invaluable data for over five decades. Today, Landsat and other Earth-observing satellites are used globally to monitor crops, wildfires, flooding, vegetation health, land use, and various other changes to the planet.
summary: Gemini Astronaut Photos Inspired Early Earth Observation Program.

title: Chandra Discovers Trigger of Outbursts from Giant Star AT 2016blu in NGC 4559
content:
Astronomers using NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory have identified the cause of repeated outbursts from a giant, unstable star designated AT 2016blu. The star is situated in the spiral galaxy NGC 4559, approximately 30 million light-years from Earth. Estimates place the mass of this volatile star at least 33 times that of the Sun.

The discovery was accompanied by an image released on Nov. 9, 2026. The visual combines X-ray data from NASA/CXC/Univ. Of Virginia/M. Aghakhanloo et al. and optical data from SDSS, with image processing by NASA/CXC/SAO/P. Edmonds.
summary: Using NASA’s Chandra X‑ray Observatory, astronomers discovered what triggers repeated outbursts from the giant, unstable star AT 2016blu in the spiral galaxy NGC 4559. The star is at least 33 times the mass of the Sun and is located about 30 million light‑years from Earth.

title: New Apple TV 4k units show YouTube app errors on launch
content:
People who received the brand‑new Apple TV 4K today reported that the YouTube app immediately displayed error messages. In the first units the app showed a black screen with a QR code and the message, “YouTube is not yet available on this device.” In other cases the app ran but a transparent red bar appeared at the bottom of the screen, stating, “YouTube app is approved for device testing only and not for production use.”

Tom Warren of The Verge tried to resolve the problem by installing the latest tvOS 27.2 update and rebooting the device, but the issue persisted. He ultimately had to uninstall and reinstall the YouTube app to restore normal functionality.
summary: Early recipients of the new Apple TV 4k reported the YouTube app displaying a black screen with a QR code or a red bar stating it is approved for device testing only. The issue for some users required installing the tvOS 27.2 update and uninstalling and reinstalling the app to resolve.

title: Camp Snap releases CS-8 Micro, a 3‑inch keychain camcorder
content:
Camp Snap has introduced the CS-8 Micro, a further miniaturized version of its screen-free digital camcorder that is smaller than the recently launched CS-8 Mini. The new device measures approximately three inches in length and weighs 1.5 ounces, allowing it to be attached to a keychain. Like its larger predecessors, the CS-8 Micro features a smaller grip designed for easy handling and can capture video using one of five built-in filters.

The CS-8 Micro will be available for purchase starting November 17th at 11AM ET. It is priced at $39.99 and can be bought through Camp Snap’s online store, Target, and Urban Outfitters.
summary: Last week, Camp Snap launched a miniaturized version of its screen-free CS-8 video camera that was half the size of the original with a smaller grip designed to be easier for kids to hold. But it turns out the company wasn't done shrinking its hardware.

title: Jensen Huang Defends Nvidia’s AI Role Amid Environmental Criticism
content:
Nvidia, under the leadership of cofounder Jensen Huang, has emerged as a central driver of the artificial intelligence boom while simultaneously becoming a significant environmental liability for the tech industry. The company’s high-demand chips have spurred the construction of new factories that are intensive in water and chemical usage. Additionally, these products have contributed to draining power grids through massive data centers and have created the potential for a future electronic waste crisis.

During a keynote address at the Berlin GPU Technology Conference on October 21st, Huang represented a company that has faced friction with environmental organizations. These groups have sought to hold Nvidia accountable for its "hidden" emissions. While Huang has promoted the use of AI as a tool to combat climate change, the source notes that the company’s supply chain emissions increased during this period.
summary: Jensen Huang gives a keynote address at the Berlin GPU Technology Conference on October 21st in Berlin. | Photo: Getty Images Under cofounder Jensen Huang, Nvidia has become the engine for the AI boom - and one of the tech industry's biggest environmental liabilities.

Keychron’s first trackball, the Nape Pro, debuted at CES 2026. The device has a slim, compact design that lets it sit right up against a keyboard.

The T1 HE also allows the trackball to be fine‑tuned with minor positional adjustments so it rests squarely under the thumb without any reaching.

The T1 HE is now available for preorder through Keychron’s online store.
summary: Keychron's new T1 HE wireless mouse features a side‑mounted 34mm trackball that can be fine‑tuned to rest squarely under the thumb, improving ergonomics. The device is now available for preorder through Keychron's online store.

content:
CMF by Nothing’s milk‑carton‑shaped Bluetooth speaker, the CMF Speaker S, has been discounted to a new low of $39 on both Amazon and Nothing’s own website. The speaker is available in four colors—white, dark gray, orange, and turquoise—and the $39 price represents a $20 reduction from its launch price, the lowest it has ever sold at since it entered the market about a month ago.

The Speaker S is the smaller of the two models in the line. It features a 45 mm driver accompanied by two passive radiators that help deliver low‑end frequencies. A single charge powers the speaker for up to 18 hours, and it carries an IP68 rating, making it resistant to water and dust.

Connectivity options include Bluetooth 6, fast pairing through multiple methods such as NFC and Google Fast Pair, and audio input via USB‑C. The speaker also supports stereo pairing with a second CMF Speaker S, allowing users to create a dual‑speaker setup.

Both the Speaker S and the larger Series M share removable faceplates and multifunction front knobs, letting owners swap colors or customize the look. CMF plans to release STL files so anyone with a 3D printer can create additional attachments or designs. The Series M is also on sale at Amazon for $79, a $30 discount from its original price.
summary: The CMF Speaker S, a milk carton-shaped Bluetooth speaker, is now available for $39 on Amazon and Nothing, a $20 discount from its original $59 price. It offers a 45mm driver, two passive radiators, 18‑hour battery life, IP68 rating, and supports stereo pairing, Bluetooth 6, NFC, Google Fast Pair, and USB‑C audio.

content:

title: It's the end of the world as we know it, per a physicist's 1960 prediction
content: As of this morning, Microsoft is still scrambling to restore service following yesterday's global outage, with millions of users unable to access Outlook and other vital tools. It's not the end of the world, but it does seem fitting that this should happen on the day a physicist predicted would be the end of humanity: November 13, 2026. And it falls on a Friday, too. The physicist in question is Heinz von Foerster, who published a 1960 paper in the journal Science predicting that by today, overpopulation would reach the breaking point. It's not a new fear. English economist Thomas Malthus —one of the early pioneers in modeling population dynamics—made a similar prediction in 1798, claiming that a rapidly growing population would eventually exhaust the available food supply, and humanity would starve to death. His model rested on the assumption of exponential growth, but the equation is only applicable under specific conditions, such as scientists growing bacteria in a lab in a perfectly controlled environment. Even then, while growth occurs exponentially for a time, it does not continue forever. Population dynamics are notoriously tricky to calculate because there are so many variables to consider and so much unpredictability in the system. In his 1960 analysis, Von Foerster accurately measured past trends in population growth, but like Malthus, he assumed those trends would carry into the future largely unchanged. So he projected that human population growth would march inexorably toward infinity. We wouldn't starve to death; von Foerster thought we would be ingenious enough to solve the food supply problem. Instead, "they will be squeezed to death," he wrote. Read full article Comments
summary: It's the end of the world as we know it, per a physicist's 1960 prediction.
author: Ars Technica

title: Microsoft 365 global outage continues, email service extended to 48 hours
content:
A global outage that began at midday on Thursday has left many Microsoft 365 services unavailable, according to reports. The disruption has affected users of Microsoft email, cloud, and AI services and remains unresolved into Friday morning.

Microsoft has released a full list of the services impacted by the error. In response, the company moved early Friday to safeguard customers worldwide from losing emails during the extended outage.

The Microsoft 365 Status account confirmed on X that “Recovery actions are ongoing” and that the company has “extended email timeout to 48 hours” to help preserve delayed mail.

title: Nightmare Eclipse releases SignDrop Windows zero‑day giving local users System rights
content:
Nightmare Eclipse, a researcher who has publicly criticized Microsoft, released a new Windows zero‑day on Tuesday. The vulnerability, dubbed SignDrop, allows local users to gain full System rights on certain Windows versions. It is located in the Common Log File System (CLFS), which Microsoft defines as a “general‑purpose logging service used by software clients running in user‑mode or kernel‑mode.”

SignDrop works by forcing a privileged process—such as Windows Defender—to open a specially crafted CLFS container. An attacker with ordinary user privileges can then exploit the privileged file‑creation capability to elevate their rights to System. The attack leverages the interaction between CLFS, Windows Defender, and Windows file permissions. Specifically, it uses the legitimate Defender function ServerMpUpdateEngineSignature, which processes antivirus signature updates, to open the malicious log file.
summary: Nightmare Eclipse, a researcher with a public dispute with Microsoft, disclosed the SignDrop vulnerability that allows local users to gain full System rights on some Windows versions. The flaw lies in the Common Log File System and exploits Windows Defender's privileged file creation to elevate privileges.
author: Ars Technica

title: OpenAI Board Member Warns AI Takeover Could Happen in Months
content: How do you think you're going to die? If you go by the current statistics for deaths in the US, it's reasonable to expect that cancer or heart disease will eventually get you. But OpenAI Foundation board member and Alignment Research Center Executive Director Paul Cristiano thinks we should all be worried about another major mortality risk. Speaking at a lecture series this week, Cristiano bluntly told the audience in a Toronto Convention Center, "I think for most people in this room, the most likely reason they will die is because of an AI accident." In the opening lecture of a three-part series, Cristiano outlined his worries about the risk of an impending "AI takeover." He defined that as a situation where goal-pursuing AI systems "call the shots in the same sense that humans today call the shots and what happens on Earth" and where any human trying to stop them "would be as ineffective as if you or me was trying to stop the US military." Such a situation would likely lead to mass death and perhaps uninhabitable environments for humans, Cristiano said. Read full article Comments
summary: OpenAI Foundation board member Paul Cristiano said that an AI accident could be the most likely cause of death for people in the room. He warned that an AI takeover could happen within months, potentially causing mass death and uninhabitable environments.
author: Ars Technica

title: Kalshi ends Donald Trump Jr.'s advisory role after his firm invests in competitor
content:
Donald Trump Jr. has agreed to end his advisory role with the prediction‑market platform Kalshi. Kalshi said the decision was mutual and followed a “significant investment” by Trump Jr.’s venture‑capital firm in Polymarket, a competitor, during the past summer. The company thanked him for his contributions in helping market Kalshi to more customers.

Kalshi noted that Trump Jr. may still retain a financial interest in the firm, which has benefited from legal and regulatory support for prediction markets under the Trump administration. According to the Financial Times, he received roughly $300,000 in equity when he joined Kalshi as a strategic adviser in early 2025. The advisory relationship has now been terminated.
summary: Donald Trump Jr. Agreed to end his advisory role with the prediction market Kalshi shortly after Trump Jr.'s venture capital firm made a large investment in its competitor, Polymarket.

title: Ministers weigh ban on under‑16s using online marketplaces after Vinted listing draws crude message
content: Ministers are weighing a ban that would stop anyone under 16 from using online marketplaces after reports of inappropriate use of messaging functions and the posting of users’ photos. One example cited involved a mother, identified as Hannah*, who listed her seven‑year‑old daughter’s pink swimming costume on Vinted for £1. The listing prompted a message from a user with a male handle that read, “So a little girl wore this yh [yeah]?” The incident highlights concerns that have prompted the proposed restriction.
summary: Ministers weigh ban on under‑16s using online marketplaces after Vinted listing draws crude message.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Pope Leo XIV leads youth prayer vigil at Lima's National Stadium
content: On Thursday, 12 November, thousands of young Catholics assembled at Peru’s National Stadium in Lima for a prayer vigil led by Pope Leo XIV. The event turned the venue into a “sea of lights,” with mobile‑phone lanterns illuminating the stands as the pontiff guided an evening of songs, prayer and reflection.
summary: Thousands of young Catholics gathered at Peru's National Stadium in Lima on Thursday 12 November for a prayer vigil led by Pope Leo XIV. The stands were illuminated by thousands of mobile phone lights as the pontiff led an evening of songs, prayer and reflection.
author: Euronews

title: Humanoid robots and robotic dogs dominate Web Summit 2026 in Lisbon
content: Dancing humanoid robots and robotic dogs were highlighted attractions at Web Summit 2026 in Lisbon. According to a study, the technology conference has generated nearly €2.5 billion for Portugal’s economy over the past decade.
summary: Dancing humanoid robots and robotic dogs stole the show at Web Summit 2026 in Lisbon. The technology conference has generated nearly €2.5 billion for Portugal's economy over the past decade, according to a study.
author: Euronews

title: Azerbaijan expands European ties at EPC Summit, pledges more energy to EU
content: At the EPC Summit Azerbaijan expanded its European outreach, announcing increased energy supplies to the EU, a strategic partnership with the United Kingdom, and further agreements with Ukraine. The delegation also held roughly a dozen bilateral talks with European leaders and convened a new meeting with Armenia to advance the historic peace process.
summary: At the EPC Summit, Azerbaijan announced increased energy supplies to the EU, a strategic partnership with the UK, and additional agreements with Ukraine. It also held a dozen bilateral meetings with European leaders and a new meeting with Armenia to advance the historic peace process.
author: Euronews

title: Euronews launches new season on Nov. 16 with more live journalism and new studio
content: Euronews will begin its new season on 16 November, introducing expanded live journalism, fresh weeknight programmes and a brand‑new studio. The network emphasizes its journalists and editorial expertise, promising additional perspectives and deeper insight into stories that shape Europe, and will deliver “more Europe than ever” across its twelve language services.
summary: Euronews is starting its new season on 16 November with more live journalism, new weeknight programmes and a brand‑new studio. The channel will provide more perspectives and deeper insight into European stories in 12 languages.
author: Euronews

title: Iran MPs debate shift in nuclear doctrine and possible NPT exit
content: Iranian parliamentarians are debating a possible shift in the country’s nuclear doctrine, including the prospect of leaving the Nuclear Non‑Proliferation Treaty. The discussion follows observations that the recent U.S. midterm elections have lowered, for now, the likelihood of a new full‑scale U.S. and Israeli attack on Iran, while the United States continues to pursue its objective of halting any Iranian nuclear programme, prompting intense debate within Iranian society and its power circles.
summary: Iran's parliament is debating a possible shift in its nuclear doctrine and an exit from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty. The US midterm elections have lowered the immediate prospect of a new full‑scale US and Israeli attack, while the US goal of halting Iran's nuclear programme fuels intense debate in Iranian society and power circles.
author: Euronews

title: France commemorates victims of 2015 Paris attacks on November 13, eleven years later
content: Eleven years after the November 13, 2015 attacks in Paris, France held a tribute ceremony. French officials, victims’ associations and families gathered on Friday to pay their respects to those killed in the attacks. The event marked the anniversary of the tragedy.
summary: Eleven years after the November 13, 2015 attacks in Paris, France held a tribute to the victims. French officials, victims’ associations and families gathered on Friday to pay their respects.
author: France 24

title: Jensen Huang resigns from Nvidia amid scandal, equities tumble
content:
Jensen Huang’s resignation from Nvidia has sparked a sharp market reaction. The departure follows allegations of extramarital affairs, alleged Chinese espionage, and a summons to testify before U.S. lawmakers.  

Investors are questioning who truly leads the tech sector and whether the substantial capital invested in AI can withstand the ensuing turmoil.
summary: Jensen Huang’s departure from Nvidia follows his resignation after extramarital affairs, alleged Chinese espionage, and a summons to testify before US lawmakers. The news caused equities to reel, raising questions about who controls tech and whether AI‑related capital can survive the turmoil.
author: France 24

title: EU AI Summit in Dublin Overshadowed by Ukraine War, Pothier Calls for More Air Defences
content:
EU leaders convened in Dublin for an AI summit, but the meeting was largely eclipsed by the ongoing war between Russia and Ukraine. William Hilderbrandt welcomed Fabrice Pothier, CEO of Rasmussen Global, to the event.

Pothier highlighted that Europe’s computing capacity represents only about 5 % of the global total. He noted that, despite a wealth of researchers and expertise, the continent struggles to translate these assets into real technological and industrial scale.

Regarding the Ukraine conflict, Pothier urged European governments to shift focus from debating their own positions to strengthening Ukraine’s capabilities, particularly by supplying additional air‑defence interceptors.
summary: EU leaders met in Dublin for an AI summit, but the meeting was largely dominated by Russia's war on Ukraine. Fabrice Pothier, CEO of Rasmussen Global, warned that Europe's computing capacity is only about 5% of the global total and urged European governments to provide more air defence interceptors to strengthen Ukraine.
author: France 24

title: Kosovo PM Albin Kurti says country has done its homework to secure EU candidate status
content: FRANCE 24 hosts Albin Kurti, the prime minister of Kosovo, a country that declared its independence from Serbia back in 2008 and sees itself as part of the European family. But four years after applying to join the EU, Kosovo has still not received candidate status. We explore Kosovo's path towards the EU, and the broader European and regional dynamics surrounding that.
summary: Albin Kurti, prime minister of Kosovo, told France 24 that Kosovo has completed its preparations to obtain EU candidate status. Kosovo declared independence from Serbia in 2008 and, four years after applying to join the EU, has not yet been granted candidate status.
author: France 24

title: China conducts major drills around Taiwan since early November, simulating blockade
content: Since early November, China has conducted major military drills around Taiwan. Social media claims of an actual blockade are unsubstantiated; Beijing's forces have only simulated a blockade, not implemented one.
summary: China has been carrying out major military drills around Taiwan since early November. Beijing's armed forces only simulated a blockade and did not actually implement one, contrary to some social media claims.
author: France 24

title: Hurry up and wait: Europe wants a place at the table, ‘must make up its mind’ over Ukraine
content:
Gavin Lee welcomed Alexander Titov, a Lecturer in Modern European History at Queen’s University Belfast and specialist on Russia, to discuss recent diplomatic developments.  

The conversation focused on high‑level meetings held in Abu Dhabi and Dublin, and on prospects for ending the war in Ukraine.
summary: Gavin Lee is pleased to welcome Alexander Titov, Lecturer in Modern European History at Queen's University Belfast and a specialist on Russia. He's joined us to discuss high-level meetings in Abu Dhabi, Dublin and the prospects for ending the war in Ukraine.
author: France 24

title: Ukraine and Russia hold first direct talks since February, US in room, Europe in lobby
content:
The podcast “The World This Week with Gavin Lee” presents a 45‑minute panel that reviews the week’s breaking news. One segment focuses on Ukraine, asking who will speak for Europe as the first direct talks between Ukraine and Russia since February take place. According to the discussion, the United States participated in the talks while Moscow reports that European representatives were confined to the lobby.

The panel also examines a proposed “European Security Architecture” that emerged during the talks. The episode’s broader agenda includes analysis of recent global developments, as framed by the host and guests.
summary: The panel on “On The World This Week with Gavin Lee” noted that Ukraine and Russia held their first direct talks since February. The United States was present while European representatives were described by Moscow as relegated to the lobby, and a new European Security Architecture was discussed.

title: Turkey and Qatar sign mutual defence pact pledging joint response to attacks
content: Turkey and Qatar signed a mutual defence agreement on Friday, pledging a unified response to any attack on either country, the two leaders said in a joint statement. The pact follows the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, which Turkey, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia signed in August.
summary: Turkey and Qatar signed a mutual defence agreement on Friday, pledging a unified response to any attack on either country. The pact follows the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement signed by Turkey, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia in August.
author: France 24

title: Czechia prepares for massive protest in Prague over public media funding cuts
content:
A fast‑tracked bill to cut public media funding has sparked strikes, rallies and fears for the independence of public broadcasting in Czechia.  
A massive protest is planned for Prague on Sunday.
summary: A fast‑tracked bill to cut public media funding has sparked strikes, rallies and fears for the independence of public broadcasting in Czechia. A massive protest is planned for Prague on Sunday.

title: Beijing Cautious About Hosting Xi-Putin-Trump Summit, Risks Global Image
content: Beijing is weighing the prospect of hosting a summit that would bring together Chinese President Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin and former U.S. President Donald Trump. Officials say the country must tread carefully, noting that while the meeting would likely benefit Moscow’s image, it could also jeopardize China’s standing on the global stage.
summary: China is forced to tread carefully as it considers hosting a meeting between Xi Jinping, Vladimir Putin, and Donald Trump. The optics favor Moscow, and Beijing risks its image at the global stage.

title: Iran says it struck US radar systems in Bahrain; US reports intercepting attacks
content: Iran said it hit United States radar systems located in Bahrain, while the United States reported that it intercepted the attacks. The confrontations persist in the Strait of Hormuz, with the broader conflict described as remaining in a state of de‑escalation.
summary: Iran claimed it struck US radar systems in Bahrain. The US said it intercepted the attacks, and clashes continue in the Strait of Hormuz as the war remains in a state of de‑escalation.

title: Haiti's Prime Minister congratulates El Salvador's President on gang crackdown in Haiti
content: Haiti’s Prime Minister recently congratulated El Salvador’s President for a gang crackdown in Haiti, a gesture that has highlighted the ties between the two countries. The article raises questions about what is happening and asks where the United States stands.
summary: Haiti's Prime Minister praised El Salvador's President for a gang crackdown in Haiti. The exchange has highlighted the bilateral relationship and prompted questions about the United States' stance.

title: Experts warn revising Europe's security could grant Moscow postwar renegotiation
content: Experts caution that altering Europe’s security architecture could fulfill Moscow’s long‑standing desire to renegotiate the continent’s post‑war security arrangements. They argue that such a revision would effectively grant Russia the opportunity to reshape the established security framework.
summary: Experts warn against revising Europe's security framework. They say it would grant Moscow its longstanding wish of renegotiating postwar security on the continent.

title: UN and partners urge rapid entry of winter aid into Gaza after deadly rain
content: Winter supplies must enter the Gaza Strip where “lives are at stake”, the UN and partners said in an urgent appeal on Friday, in the wake of deadly rainfall this past weekend.
summary: The UN and partners issued an urgent appeal on Friday urging that winter supplies be allowed into the Gaza Strip. The appeal came after deadly rainfall this past weekend, which put lives at stake.

title: COP31 finance talks fall short, pressure builds on polluters to pay
content: At COP31 on Friday, finance dominated the agenda, with discussions spanning emotional appeals for climate justice and high‑stakes negotiations over billions of dollars. UN Secretary‑General António Guterres warned that even tripling adaptation funding for vulnerable countries would meet less than a third of their needs, as pressure mounted on wealthy nations and major polluters to pay their fair share.
summary: Finance dominated the discussions at COP31 on Friday. UN Secretary‑General António Guterres warned that even tripling adaptation funding for vulnerable countries would meet less than a third of their needs, as pressure mounted on wealthy nations and major polluters to pay their fair share.

title: Security Council meets on threats to Hormuz shipping as Iran nearly closes strait
content:
Nearly nine months after Israeli and U.S. strikes on Iran set off a regional war, the Gulf remains on a knife edge. Iran has almost closed the Strait of Hormuz, which carried a fifth of the world’s oil before the conflict.

Attacks on shipping are rising, and efforts to stop a return to full‑scale fighting have yet to produce a deal.

The Security Council is meeting at Bahrain’s request to discuss the threat to regional and maritime security. Follow live below – and for full meetings coverage year round, go here.
summary: The Security Council is meeting at Bahrain’s request to discuss the threat to regional and maritime security. Iran has all but closed the Strait of Hormuz and attacks on shipping are rising nine months after Israeli and US strikes on Iran.
author: UN News

title: Create Streets report urges removing clutter, restricting cars to revive UK high streets
content:
The urban thinktank Create Streets has released a report suggesting that UK high streets could be revitalized through low-cost interventions rather than expensive multimillion-pound revamps. The exclusive report argues that restricting car access and freeing up pavement space are effective ways to make town and city centres more appealing to shoppers.

This proposal addresses the long-standing decline of the high street, a challenge that has concerned British governments for years. By focusing on smaller changes to remove clutter, the thinktank posits that local authorities can improve the environment for shoppers without incurring significant costs.
summary: The urban thinktank Create Streets released a report saying that restricting cars and freeing up pavement space could be a cheap way to entice shoppers to UK high streets. The report argues that smaller changes, rather than multimillion‑pound revamps, could make town and city centres more appealing.
author: Guardian World

title: Walliams allegations spark calls for staggered consent age of 16 and 17
content:
Calls for a staggered age of consent have intensified after allegations against Russell Brand and David Walliams, the latter of whom denies the claims. A barrister has argued that current law does not adequately recognise the power imbalance between young people and older adults. The allegations have prompted demands for stronger legal protection for 16‑ and 17‑year‑olds against sexual exploitation by older adults.  

Campaigners favour a staggered consent law, a position that has gained support from some Labour MPs. Claire Waxman, the victims’ commissioner for England and Wales, has urged “serious conversations” about the possibility of legislative change.
summary: Walliams allegations spark calls for staggered consent age of 16 and 17.
