title: Probation officers in England and Wales vote to strike over pay, workloads
content:
Probation officers across England and Wales voted to strike over pay and excessive workloads, a move that could begin on 23 November. Members of the union Napo supported overtime restrictions and other actions short of a full strike.

The vote came as the government’s plans to release thousands of prisoners early to ease overcrowding face a setback. Napo is also preparing for additional strike action at a later stage.
summary: Probation officers in England and Wales voted to strike over pay and excessive workloads, with the strike likely to begin on 23 November. Union members of Napo also backed overtime restrictions and other actions short of a strike, dealing a blow to the government's plan to release thousands of prisoners early.
author: Guardian World

title: US Air Force responds to suspected unauthorized drone activity at RAF Lakenheath
content: The U.S. Air Force said it responded to “suspected unauthorised drone activity” on Friday night at RAF Lakenheath, an airbase in the east of England’s Suffolk county. The service reported that no personnel, aircraft or infrastructure at the site were affected.
summary: The US Air Force said it responded to suspected unauthorized drone activity on Friday night at RAF Lakenheath in eastern England. It added that no personnel, aircraft or infrastructure were affected.
author: Guardian World

title: Iran's IRGC says it destroyed US early-warning radar in Bahrain in retaliation
content:
Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) announced that it has targeted and destroyed a U.S. early‑warning radar in Bahrain. The strike, described as the first direct attack on U.S. military installations in months, was said to be retaliation for a U.S. airstrike on a communications tower in Sirik that overlooks the Strait of Hormuz.

The IRGC characterized the action as a “serious warning” to the United States, urging an end to what it called “aerial mischief and oil smuggling” in the strait. It added that its aerospace force is on full alert and prepared to confront any further violations or aggression.
summary: Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps says it has targeted and destroyed a US early‑warning radar in Bahrain in response to a US airstrike on a communications tower in Sirik overlooking the strait of Hormuz. It is Iran’s first direct attack on US military installations for months.
author: Guardian World

title: UK-EU post‑Brexit deal to cut £60m annual plant‑trade costs, says Environment Secretary Eagle
content:
The UK and EU will sign an agreement next week aimed at smoothing the movement of food, plants and animals, removing border checks and paperwork on plant imports. Environment Secretary Angela Eagle said the change will “dissolve” £60 million of annual costs for the horticulture industry, though it will not enable firms to recover the large sums already spent on border‑control compliance.

Eagle added that she hopes the paperwork headaches for importers will “disappear” after the changes, even as the upcoming UK‑EU summit on 20 November approaches.
summary: The new UK‑EU agreement will remove border checks and paperwork on plant imports, eliminating about £60 million of annual costs for the horticulture industry, the environment secretary Angela Eagle said. Eagle added that while paperwork headaches should disappear, the changes will not enable businesses to recover the large sums they previously spent on border controls.
author: Guardian World

title: AI uncovers hundreds of theorems in Kurt Gödel's 1,009-page notebooks
content:
AI is now being used to unlock discoveries hidden in the notebooks of Kurt Gödel, the Austrian logician who transformed mathematics. The notebooks contain 1,009 pages of densely written text, much of it in an obsolete shorthand, and are said to hold hundreds of proved theorems.

Gödel’s two incompleteness theorems, published in 1931, revolutionised mathematics and paved the way for the digital age. After these seminal results of the 1930s, he published only a few papers. His unpublished work, however, runs to tens of thousands of pages and remains of great interest to historians of science.
summary: AI is being used to examine Kurt Gödel's 1,009 pages of densely written notes, many in an obsolete shorthand, which are said to contain hundreds of proved theorems. Gödel, the Austrian logician whose 1931 incompleteness theorems transformed mathematics, left tens of thousands of unpublished pages that interest historians of science.
author: Guardian World

title: Former Hamas bodyguard convicted of Birmingham knife attack also wanted in Germany
content:
Mohammed Alfatih, also known as Mohammed Naim, was found guilty on Friday of a knife attack on a bailiff outside his home in Birmingham. The court convicted the former Hamas bodyguard of the Birmingham knife crime.

While detained for the bailiff attack, Alfatih was rearrested on allegations of a plot to target Israelis in Europe. German authorities have also listed him as wanted for an alleged plan to murder Jewish people. Details of the alleged plot can now be reported.
summary: Former Hamas bodyguard Mohammed Alfatih, also known as Mohammed Naim, was found guilty on Friday of a knife attack on a bailiff outside his home in Birmingham. He is also wanted in Germany for an alleged plot to murder Jewish people and target Israelis in Europe.

title: 12 12 12 review – Anthony Mackie and Jamie Dornan’s super fun heist hunt
content:
The new eight-episode heist thriller 12 12 12 opens with a contortionist emerging from a safety deposit box in an underground Swiss bank vault. The character lands on his hands and displaced knees, an opening that the review describes as immediately captivating. The series stars Anthony Mackie and Jamie Dornan as antagonists engaged in an international cat-and-mouse game.

The review notes that Mackie is known for his work in the Marvel Cinematic Universe, while Dornan has built a career since the 2013 series The Fall. The critic suggests viewers suspend their disbelief to enjoy the show, describing the 12-day hunt for the culprits as a thrilling ride. The piece concludes with a humorous observation regarding the difficulty of extending the series to twelve episodes.
summary: 12 12 12 review – Anthony Mackie and Jamie Dornan’s super fun heist hunt.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Snoh Aalegra's 'Legendary Love' review: raw R&B talent restrained by reverence for the greats
content: (Stem) Her truly remarkable, Sade-ish voice is hypnotic against some dizzyingly plush production, but a modern spin on 80s pastiche sometimes veers too close to tribute Swedish-Iranian singer Snoh Aalegra has previously described her music – a lush, pastiche-y mix of R&B, hip-hop, soul and pop – as “cinematic soul”. But although she’s a dab hand at graceful, timeless presentation (and has a truly remarkable voice) Aalegra’s music has often struggled to match up to its aesthetic, hampered by her love of the greats and a penchant for broadly generic lyrics. Her most recent album, 2021’s Temporary Highs in the Violet Skies, made some headway toward carving out a more distinctive sound, thanks to sparky and inventive production from Tyler, the Creator, No ID, P2J and the Neptunes, but still didn’t quite feel like the right fit. Aalegra’s fourth album is her most successful front-to-back statement yet, even if she can’t shake off the talent-show-ish reverence for her idols. Sparse and warm, Legendary Love puts her androgynous, Sade-ish voice in dizzyingly plush environments: a hybrid of Afrobeats and 80s R&B on the hypnotic I Love You ; a bed of minimalist guitars and moonlit synths on This That, which sounds as though it could have been produced by Jai Paul.
summary: The review describes Snoh Aalegra's fourth album, 'Legendary Love', as her most successful front-to-back statement yet, featuring sparse and warm production. Despite her remarkable voice, the album is noted for being hampered by a talent-show-ish reverence for her idols and a modern spin on 80s pastiche.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Amazon MGM Studios Prepares to Announce Next James Bond After $1bn Acquisition
content:
Amazon MGM Studios is preparing to announce the next actor to portray James Bond, a decision that follows the studio’s acquisition of creative control for over $1 billion from Barbara Broccoli and Michael G Wilson. Although no official announcement has been made, reports indicate that the shortlist to replace Daniel Craig has narrowed to five candidates: Callum Turner, Jack Lowden, Josh O’Connor, Robert Pattinson, and Nicholas Hoult. Craig previously stepped down from the role after completing No Time to Die, a film in which the character appeared to be killed in a missile strike.

This transition occurs as the franchise marks its 25th official film, excluding the two “unofficial” entries Casino Royale (1967) and Never Say Never Again (1983). The article notes that the manner in which the news is delivered is critical, referencing past instances of logistical errors, such as double bookings and health and safety issues, that have complicated previous casting announcements.
summary: Amazon MGM Studios is preparing to announce the next actor to play James Bond, with a shortlist reportedly including Callum Turner, Jack Lowden, Josh O’Connor, Robert Pattinson, and Nicholas Hoult. The studio acquired creative control of the franchise for over $1 billion from Barbara Broccoli and Michael G Wilson following Daniel Craig's departure.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Netflix’s The Body: 2004 Catholic school drama features Satanic rituals
content:
Netflix’s new YA drama, The Body, is a camp coming-of-age story set in 2004 at St Mark’s Catholic school. The narrative centers on the school’s social hierarchy, led by the dance troupe known as the Lions, who are presided over by best friends Anya and Elise. Meanwhile, homeschooled siblings Lisbeth and Leo, who live with their unwell mother, exist as outcasts. Lisbeth seeks to integrate with the popular crowd when she is invited to a Halloween party held at an abandoned convent called Devil’s House.

Lisbeth attends the event dressed as “Slutty God” but is disappointed to find that a vacant spot on the Lions team has been taken by Grace, the devout niece of the school’s priest. The evening turns chaotic during an ecstasy-fueled initiation ritual involving Satanic elements. As a result, Grace falls into a coma, while the other Lions begin experiencing hallucinations and seizures. These events disrupt the established social equilibrium of the school.
summary: The Body is a coming-of-age drama set in 2004 at St Mark’s Catholic school, focusing on the social hierarchy between popular students and outcasts. A Halloween party at an abandoned convent turns dangerous when an initiation ritual leaves a student comatose and others experiencing hallucinations.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Heartland Review: Jessica Chastain's Netflix Thriller Fails to Hit
content: The Oscar winner plays a singer turned detective searching for her niece in an overly generic Nashville-based mystery that fails to find its footing Given the popularity of its music and the streaming services’ interest in faith-based programming, I’m always a little surprised that there aren’t more movies and TV shows about Nashville. Well, at least the idea of Nashville, the country music mecca that is perpetually struggling to define itself within and against the country at large, a place that has always been more diverse than its reputation yet still stands for a certain image of white, Christian Americana. There are plenty of enduring contradictions to mine there – the hyper-masculine men singing with their hearts on their sleeve, the Madonna-badass complex among its relatively few female stars, the suburban money in a genre ostensibly speaking to the rural common man. Netflix seems to be aiming for some of those complexities with Heartland, a patchy neo-noir thriller starring Jessica Chastain as a washed-up former star turned vigilante detective with an axe to grind on Music Row. Chastain’s Misty Jones is certainly a thorny Nashville archetype, a female lead we might call “unlikable” painted in the stark terms of a bad country song (said with love as someone raised on country radio). The first five minutes of the nearly two-hour feature from Shana Feste, the writer-director perhaps best known for the 2010 movie Country Strong that launched Gwyneth Paltrow’s brief singing career, churn through the greatest hits of on-screen female fuck-up: teary loneliness, near-wordless pick-up of a stranger from the bar, beer bottle on the nightstand, joint in the bathroom, haunting echoes of erstwhile better days (in this case, a Grammy in an empty fridge, which does feel inspired in its bluntness).
summary: Jessica Chastain, an Oscar winner, stars in Netflix's Heartland as a former singer turned detective searching for her niece in a generic Nashville mystery. The film is called a patchy neo-noir thriller that fails to find its footing.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Revived art prize gives football its creative due once more
content:
Football and the art world have historically maintained a distance, with the sport being a rare subject for artists in its early decades. Notable exceptions include Umberto Boccioni’s 1913 painting Dynamism of a Soccer Player, Kazimir Malevich’s Painterly Realism of a Football Player – Color Masses in the 4th Dimension, and a smoggy scene titled Any Wintry Afternoon in England currently displayed at the Manchester Art Gallery. These works remained isolated instances of football appearing in fine art.

In 1953, the Football Association launched an art prize supported by the newly formed Arts Council. The winning works included L.S. Lowry’s Going To The Match, which depicts crowds heading to Bolton Wanderers’ then-home ground, Burnden Park. An exhibition of the submissions, titled Football and The Fine Arts, toured the country. The FA secretary, Sir Stanley Rous, expressed hope that the initiative would finally break the barrier between football and the art world. This year’s award entries indicate a healthy revival of this creative intersection.
summary: The breadth of entries for this year's award reveals a healthy revival in the relationship between football and the art world. The Football Association launched an art prize in 1953, backed by the newly formed Arts Council, to break the barrier between those two worlds.
author: Guardian Sport

title: England defeat France 50-38 to defend Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup title
content:
England’s men’s wheelchair rugby league team successfully defended their World Cup title by defeating France 50-38 in the final held in Wollongong. Joe Coyd scored four tries during the match, contributing to the historic victory. The result extends England’s dominance in the sport, as the English and French teams have shared the previous four World Cup titles between them.

The final highlighted the strong rivalry between the two nations, which have produced intense encounters on the field. Off the field, the teams maintain a relationship characterized by great respect. The sport is noted for allowing disabled and able-bodied athletes to compete alongside one another, a dynamic that underlines the positives of the wheelchair game.
summary: England's men's wheelchair rugby league team won the World Cup final in Wollongong by defeating France 50-38. Joe Coyd scored four tries during the match, which marked a successful title defence for the English team.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Debutant Mahli Beardman takes six wickets as Australia beats England in ODI
content: A week of watching Australian cricket descend into civil war ended with smiles being wiped from English faces after a stunning debut from fast bowler Mahli Beardman consigned the tourists to an all-too-familiar hammering in Perth. Victory in a low-key one-day international was never going to atone for the galling start to that failed Ashes campaign here 12 months ago. Nevertheless, England appeared better prepared this time, while the hosts were missing their big three quicks and fighting sandpaper-related bushfires off the field. And yet by 4.38pm local time – nine hours after Pat Cummins had finished his marathon takedown of Usman Khawaja’s autobiography in Sydney – Harry Brook’s side were 1-0 down once again. Rolled for 131 all out in just 33.4 overs, having been 68 for eight at one stage, a seven-wicket loss was the upshot. There was more than a touch of Cummins about their tormentor on the day, too, with Beardman claiming figures of six for 24 from 7.4 overs in his first ODI – a new national record, no less. Just 21 years old, but already touching 90mph on the speed gun, the Western Australian looks a considerable prospect. Much like Cummins, Beardman has been mentored by the great Dennis Lillee and endured battles with a rebellious body along the way. Even with a first-class debut still pending, it would not be a shock to see him handed a baggy green cap in the coming months or travel to England for the Ashes next year.
summary: Twenty-one-year-old Australian fast bowler Mahli Beardman took a career-best six for 24 in his first ODI to lead Australia to a seven-wicket victory over England in Perth. England was bowled out for 131 all out in 33.4 overs, suffering a defeat that left them trailing 1-0 in the series.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Commerce Secretary Lutnick Agrees to Testify on Nvidia Spy Scandal
content: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has agreed to voluntarily testify before the Senate Banking Committee. content: Siberian rubythroat was thousands of miles off course from its route to winter in south or south-east Asia A bird that flies south from its breeding grounds in Siberia to winter in south and south-east Asia has been found thousands of miles off course in Cumbria. Regrettably, it was found by a cat. Chris Hind, Cumbria’s county recorder for birds, said it was “extraordinary” that a Siberian rubythroat was found on his patch, albeit dead. There have been only 17 recorded instances of the bird in the UK, 15 of those in the northern Scottish isles.
summary: A Siberian rubythroat was found dead in Cumbria after being killed by a cat, having strayed thousands of miles from its expected route to Asia. The sighting is considered extraordinary, as there have been only 17 recorded instances of this bird in the UK.

title: Norway court invalidates oil permits as Guterres warns against building peace on burning planet
content: Debate over climate science, transition away from fossil fuels, electrification and climate finance can begin in earnest as world leaders leave UN summit Far away from the conference centre, Norway’s supreme court has declared the state’s decision to award three permits for oil and gasfields in the North Sea invalid, as it had not accounted for the harm caused by burning the fuels. The decision, hailed as a win by climate campaigners, does not automatically revoke the permits or demand an immediate shutdown of the fields, but will force the government to consider the global impacts of pollution before awarding licenses. It comes two days after the Norwegian prime minister, Jonas Gahr Stør, told fellow leaders at Cop31 that “Norway will do its part” in a speech that did not mention the country’s ongoing expansion of oil and gas infrastructure.

title: Seneca Meadows landfill in New York to be raised beyond Statue of Liberty height
content:
New York is running out of space for its waste, even with a landfill the size of the Statue of Liberty. The state’s largest active dump, Seneca Meadows, already reaches about 300 feet high—roughly the height of the Statue of Liberty—and covers 350 acres of deposited trash. Since the 1980s the site has expanded to its current size.

Operators of the landfill are proposing to extend its life by raising the mound even further. The plan has drawn consternation from nearby residents, who worry about the continued growth of the site and its pungent odor. The landfill sits in the scenic Finger Lakes region in northern New York.
summary: The Seneca Meadows landfill in New York's Finger Lakes region covers 350 acres and rises to about 300 feet, roughly the height of the Statue of Liberty. Operators plan to raise the landfill further, a proposal that has caused consternation among nearby residents.

title: Nature's cheaper climate adaptation: mangroves, forests, urban trees vs concrete and steel
content:
The conventional approach to climate adaptation relies on concrete and steel structures, such as seawalls, dikes, dams, and drainage systems. While these engineered solutions can be effective, they are characterized as expensive and inflexible.

An alternative strategy that receives significantly less attention involves using natural elements like mangroves, forests, and urban trees. These nature-based solutions offer a much cheaper option for protecting humans, their homes, farms, and cities from threats including floods, droughts, rising seas, and heat.
summary: The default for climate adaptation is to build concrete and steel structures such as seawalls, dikes, dams, and drainage systems. Mangroves, forests and urban trees offer a cheaper alternative that protects people, homes, farms and cities from floods, droughts, rising seas and heat.

title: MIT study finds sleep CSF waste‑clearing waves impaired in older adults
content:
MIT researchers have identified a decline in a brain‑cleansing process that occurs during sleep in older adults. The study, published today in Nature Aging, shows that waves of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) that help flush waste from the brain are markedly reduced in people aged 60 to 84 compared with younger adults. The impairment is linked to a decrease in the slow brain waves that normally dominate deep, non‑REM sleep, and the researchers emphasize that it is not simply a consequence of shorter sleep duration.

The investigation recruited two age groups—18 to 39 and 60 to 84—and conducted two‑hour overnight scans that began late at night to encourage sleep. Participants underwent functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), a modified MRI technique developed by senior author Laura Lewis to measure CSF flow, and electroencephalography (EEG) to monitor brain activity. Many subjects fell asleep in the scanner, allowing the team to compare awake and sleeping states. In the younger cohort, the EEG slow waves intensified during non‑REM sleep and the accompanying CSF waves enlarged. In contrast, older participants exhibited CSF waves that were significantly smaller than those seen in the younger group.

To probe the mechanisms behind the age‑related decline, the researchers performed additional awake‑state experiments. They assessed neurovascular coupling by presenting a flickering checkerboard, a stimulus that normally increases neural activity and blood flow. While older subjects showed neural activation, their blood flow response was blunted, indicating diminished vascular responsiveness. A breath‑hold challenge further revealed that older participants had a smaller increase in cerebral blood flow than younger subjects. These two factors explained much, but not all, of the reduced CSF flow, suggesting other age‑related contributors.

The study also noted that some older adults displayed gray‑matter atrophy, which correlated with a greater decrease in CSF flow. While none of the participants had a diagnosed neurodegenerative disorder, the researchers plan to follow individuals longitudinally to determine whether altered CSF dynamics predict future risk. They are also exploring interventions, such as brief bursts of pink noise during sleep, that previously increased CSF flow in younger adults, and aim to test whether such approaches could benefit older participants.

The research was funded by the National Institutes of Health, the Simons Collaboration on Plasticity in the Aging Brain, a McKnight Scholar Award, a Pew Biomedical Scholar Award, an MIT EECS Transformative Research Award, the Picower Institute Neurological Disorder Discovery Research Fund, a Sloan Fellowship, and the Department of Defense National Defense Science and Engineering Graduate Fellowship Program. The lead authors are Sydney Bailes, a postdoc in the MIT Laboratory for Information and Decision Systems, and Stephanie Williams, a former visiting student who earned a PhD from Boston University in 2026. Laura Lewis, the Athinoula A. Martinos Associate Professor of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, is the senior author.
summary: As people age, they may sleep for shorter periods and wake up more frequently during the night. In addition to those disruptions, MIT researchers have now discovered that a process responsible for flushing waste from the brain during sleep is commonly impaired in older people.

title: The Sun unleashed a monster storm. Earth may have made it worse
content: The May 2024 solar storm, which illuminated skies worldwide, revealed that Earth’s upper atmosphere contributed significantly to the disturbance's intensity. Satellite measurements indicated that approximately 85% of the charged particles fueling the event originated from the planet's own atmosphere rather than the solar wind. Additionally, scientists detected an extraordinary 40% weakening of Earth's magnetic field at high altitudes.

title: Study of 750,000 pregnancies reveals a surprising twist about Ozempic and Wegovy
content: A study analyzing over 750,000 pregnancies found that early exposure to Ozempic, Wegovy, and similar drugs was not linked to increased pregnancy complications when used for weight loss. However, the research indicated a higher risk of premature birth when these medications were prescribed for diabetes. This distinction suggests that diabetes itself may be driving the observed risk, though researchers caution that the safety of these drugs during pregnancy remains uncertain.
summary: Study of 750,000 pregnancies reveals a surprising twist about Ozempic and Wegovy.

content: Scientists have identified that superheated magma can delay crystal formation for over eight hours, compared to just 20 minutes in non-superheated magma. This hidden effect of extreme heat may explain why some volcanoes erupt with spectacular lava fountains while others release lava more quietly.
summary: Why do some volcanoes erupt with spectacular lava fountains while others release lava more quietly? Scientists have discovered that a hidden effect of extreme heat inside magma may help explain the difference.

title: Friday 13th superstition lowers property prices and airfares
content:
The date of Friday the 13th is associated with various negative economic and social trends, including lower median prices for property sales, cheaper airfares, a lack of weddings, and an increase in motor collisions. This day is widely perceived as unlucky, leading many individuals to avoid scheduling significant events such as job interviews, elective surgeries, or flights.

Caroline Smyth, a photographer and celebrant based in Larne, Northern Ireland, noted that she has only worked one Friday the 13th wedding in her 14 years of business. She attributes this avoidance to the date being surrounded by superstition, suggesting that people may fear it is a bad omen for their marriage. Smyth’s single Friday the 13th wedding, which took place in September 2013, was the first she ever photographed and helped launch her career. Despite this positive outcome for Smyth, the date remains largely avoided by others who believe it brings bad luck.
summary: Property sales completing on Friday 13th have a lower median price, while airfares are cheaper and motor collisions increase. Many people avoid booking significant events like weddings or job interviews on this date due to superstition.

title: Silicon Valley Misreads Politics; Nvidia Confirms Chip Tracking for Smuggling
content:
Silicon Valley’s relationship with the political landscape has come under scrutiny following the midterm elections, which occurred five weeks after many tech leaders gathered at the White House to endorse President Trump’s “Super Intelligence” agenda. Aaron Zamost, a tech communications consultant and former executive at Square, notes that despite growing opposition to AI and data centers, these self-styled visionaries chose to align themselves with the administration. This decision is described as a catastrophic misreading of the political environment, raising questions about the judgment of tech leaders who have built careers on the premise of seeing the future. The alignment has potentially jeopardized the fates of their companies while challenging the perception of their foresight.

In a separate development regarding chip security, Nvidia representatives privately confirmed to Illinois Representative Bill Foster that the company could implement anti-smuggling measures required by the Chip Security Act. Foster, a Democrat and cosponsor of the act, told MIT Technology Review on Thursday that these measures are feasible, contradicting previous claims by an industry group that such requirements were “potentially infeasible.” The Chip Security Act proposes geotracking requirements to verify the location of advanced AI chips and prevent their smuggling to China. This legislative effort has gained renewed attention following the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and reports of an affair.

Meanwhile, volunteers participating in brain implant trials are advocating for greater autonomy and transparency in their research participation. Ian Burkhart, who had a brain implant in 2014, is working on guidelines for ethical trials that respect participants’ rights, including the ability to access their own brain data at any time. Burkhart argues that volunteers, who play a vital role in developing devices that can control robotic limbs, computers, and even speech, should be recognized for their contributions. These guidelines aim to reduce the reliance on non-disclosure agreements and ensure that participants retain control over their personal data.

The newsletter also highlights a major Microsoft outage that disrupted services worldwide, affecting Outlook, Teams, and Copilot. Microsoft has stated that the disruption is not a cybersecurity incident. In the aftermath of Jensen Huang’s resignation, discussions have emerged regarding his successor, with Donald Trump publicly backing Apple’s Tim Cook for the role on Truth Social. Additionally, an Alice Huang-linked firm reportedly procured banned Nvidia chips in China, with the servers initially sold to an Nvidia partner in Singapore. This incident has heightened scrutiny on Singapore’s chip links to China and raised concerns about the security of Chinese AI infrastructure.

Other notable technology stories include advocacy groups suing five frontier AI labs—Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI, and SpaceXSI—to halt development, and parents demanding an AI moratorium in schools following allegations that Gemini encouraged a teenager to plan suicide. In engineering news, a robot has assembled a structure in space for the first time, marking a step toward in-orbit manufacturing. Furthermore, SpaceX has denied throttling Ukraine’s Starshield network, despite claims by Ukrainian President Zelenskyy that such curbs are hampering drone defenses.
summary: Silicon Valley leaders misread the political landscape by supporting President Trump’s “Super Intelligence” agenda despite growing opposition to AI and data centers. Nvidia confirmed it can track chips to fight smuggling, a measure requested by the Chip Security Act, according to representatives to Illinois representative Bill Foster.
author: MIT Tech Review

content:

The new logo is a nostalgic nod to the old light‑up designs that Apple began phasing out in 2015 and had disappeared entirely by the 2018 redesign of the MacBook Air. The company has revived the feature for the current model.

title: Meta's 2023 plan to target Jonathan Haidt exposed in court filings
content:
Meta’s internal strategy to undermine social‑media critic Jonathan Haidt came to light through recent court filings in California.  The documents show that, in 2023, Meta employees discussed a “Whisper strategy” aimed at turning academics against Haidt, who is preparing a bestselling book that argues platforms like Meta’s are harming children.  

The plan was revealed last month, prompting backlash from both Haidt and his critics.  The revelation has backfired, with many of Haidt’s opponents now expressing frustration toward Meta for the attempt to influence public opinion.  

Haidt, the author of Anxious Generation, has spent years popularizing his theory that social media and smartphones adversely affect young people.  The court filings confirm that Meta had considered a covert campaign to shift academic sentiment against him.
summary: California court filings revealed that Meta employees in 2023 discussed a "Whisper strategy" to turn academics against Jonathan Haidt, who was about to publish a bestselling book criticizing social media's impact on children. The disclosure has backfired, angering both Haidt and his critics.
author: The Verge

title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns, sparking concerns over China ties and AI stability
content:
The Vergecast released a new episode that focuses on the recent developments surrounding Nvidia’s chief executive, Jensen Huang. According to the show’s description, Huang stepped down from his role as head of the company on Thursday, ending one phase of a broader saga that has drawn considerable attention.

The hosts, David and Nilay, indicate that the discussion will move beyond Huang’s resignation to examine Nvidia’s business activities in China, the United States government’s approach to the company, and potential implications for the overall stability of the artificial‑intelligence sector. The episode promises to explore these interconnected issues and how they may shape the industry in the weeks and months ahead.
summary: One part of the saga surrounding Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang ended on Thursday, when Huang resigned from his position at the top of AI's most important company. But in the coming weeks and months, a much bigger story may be about to unfold.
author: The Verge

title: Specialized Tarmac SL9 S-Level pushes riders out of Zone 2 training
content:
Specialized’s Tarmac SL9 S‑Level, the company’s aero road bike that sits just below the S‑Works tier, has been described by a rider as a model that can turn a typical Zone 2 effort into a faster, more tempo‑like ride. The author notes that the bike’s design and performance cues encourage a “go fast” mindset, making it tempting to exceed the intended steady‑state intensity of a Zone 2 workout.

The Tarmac SL9 S‑Level replaces the previous Tarmac SL8 Pro and received an update earlier this year. After the update, the writer logged nearly 1,000 miles on the bike, observing that its responsiveness and speed‑focused geometry make it rewarding to ride at higher intensities.

Specialized offers the Tarmac SL9 in four distinct models, each available with either SRAM or Shimano drivetrain groupsets. The article points out that the top‑of‑the‑line groupset can be paired with any model, and it highlights a weight difference: the Shimano version of the Expert build is 20 g lighter than its SRAM counterpart, while the Shimano Comp version is 70 g heavier than the SRAM version.

Overall, the piece emphasizes the Tarmac SL9 S‑Level’s aerodynamic focus and its ability to entice riders to push beyond a traditional Zone 2 pace, while also detailing the bike’s model range and drivetrain options.
summary: Specialized Tarmac SL9 S-Level pushes riders out of Zone 2 training.
author: Ars Technica

title: SpaceX to attempt full recovery of Starship; Rocket Lab's Electron set for 100th launch
content:
Edition 9.19 of the Rocket Report notes that SpaceX plans a historic test flight of its Starship vehicle from Starbase, Texas, on Friday. The company will attempt to recover the entire orbital rocket for reuse, followed by an upper‑stage landing attempt 22.5 hours later on Saturday afternoon, local time. The report says Ars will be on site to cover the event.

The same edition highlights a milestone for Rocket Lab’s Electron launcher. The next Electron mission is scheduled to lift off from the Mahia Peninsula in New Zealand on 14 November at 05:30 UTC, marking the vehicle’s 100th overall flight since its first launch in 2017. The newsletter invites reader submissions and encourages subscription for future issues.
summary: SpaceX will launch Starship on Friday and try to recover all components, with an upper‑stage landing attempt 22.5 hours later on Saturday. Rocket Lab plans to launch its Electron rocket on November 14 from New Zealand, marking the vehicle’s 100th mission.
author: Ars Technica

title: Slate Auto offers $25,000 electric truck with no infotainment, includes spiral road atlas
content: Whether it's nostalgia or a sense that technology has gotten a bit too pervasive, there’s no denying that Slate Auto appears to be tuned into the particular moment. The startup has a simple pitch : an affordable electric truck with just the basics, leaving owners to DIY and BYOD for everything else, all for a sub-$25,000 starting price. Among the things Slate does without is an embedded infotainment system. The small digital display on the dashboard that shows your speed and range is also where the backup camera appears if you engage reverse, and there are two USB-C ports that provide power but not connectivity, and that’s that. But there is a solution to getting lost, and it's called “Screenless GPS.” Even though we don’t have a Slate truck to test it with, the OEM sent us a unit to review. That’s right, it’s a good old spiral-bound road atlas! “We believe you should use the devices you know and love,” Slate says, and it reckons that maps worked just fine for past generations, so they should still work now. Read full article Comments
summary: Slate Auto markets an affordable electric truck priced under $25,000 that provides only basic features and omits an embedded infotainment system. Instead of a digital navigation screen, the company supplies a spiral‑bound road atlas as its “Screenless GPS” solution.
author: Ars Technica

title: Microsoft day-long Outlook and Teams outage expands to global cloud service disruption
content: Microsoft experienced a day‑long outage that started with Outlook and Teams and expanded to affect much of its cloud services, prompting the company to describe the incident as a full‑blown global cloud crisis. Microsoft reported that service is being restored gradually.
summary: Microsoft experienced a day-long outage that started with Outlook and Teams and affected many of its cloud services. The company says it is gradually restoring service.
author: TechCrunch

title: University campuses drop Flock Safety surveillance contracts after student protests
content:
Students across the United States are pressuring schools to end contracts with surveillance‑camera maker Flock Safety after privacy concerns were raised about the company’s automated license‑plate readers. At Stanford University, 21‑year‑old senior Angela Nguyen, a computer‑science major, organized a petition that gathered hundreds of signatures from students, faculty, alumni and local residents urging the university to terminate its Flock contract and establish safeguards for future technology use.

Stanford discontinued its agreement with Flock this summer. Since April, at least ten campuses in seven states have also ended contracts with the firm, including Cornell University, Penn State University, Elgin Community College, Emory University, Binghamton University, Kent State University and the University of Wisconsin’s Madison, Milwaukee and Oshkosh campuses. 

Most recently, the University at Buffalo announced an indefinite pause on a planned 60‑day pilot program involving Flock’s equipment. The wave of cancellations reflects a growing privacy reckoning over the use of such surveillance tools on college grounds.
summary: Stanford University ended its contract with Flock Safety after a campaign led by senior Angela Nguyen, who gathered hundreds of signatures to oppose automated license‑plate readers. Since April, at least ten campuses in seven states—including Cornell, Penn State, Emory and University of Buffalo—have terminated or paused their Flock contracts.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Tesla to end Cybertruck production next year, citing shift to Cybercab robotaxis
content: Eccentric and overhyped, Tesla’s Cybertruck became a stand-in for Elon Musk during his ascent in the Republican party. It will join the ranks of other vehicles symbolic of their eras – for better or for worse Three days after a historic blue tsunami changed America’s political landscape, Elon Musk announced Tesla would end production of its hulking Cybertruck next year. Was it a coincidence? Maybe. Musk said the move was “to make room for increased Cybercab production”, referring to Tesla’s Robotaxi. But the combined circumstances felt highly appropriate: it was the end of an era.
summary: Elon Musk announced Tesla will cease production of the Cybertruck next year. He said the decision is to make room for increased Cybercab production for the company's Robotaxi service.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Microsoft outage persists after 18 hours, millions still affected worldwide
content:
Microsoft says it is “continuing to see improvements in service availability” after a global outage that has disrupted Outlook, Teams and other email systems for millions of customers worldwide. The disruption, which has lasted more than 18 hours, has primarily affected the sending and receiving of email, while many essential services remain unaffected.

The Australian Medical Association reported no indications that hospitals or clinics have been impacted. Western Australia and other jurisdictions around the world are experiencing the outage, and officials say they are receiving updates from the Commonwealth, which is working with Microsoft at senior levels. Microsoft has indicated that it is prioritising life‑safety and government services as it works to resolve the issue.
summary: Microsoft reports it is “continuing to see improvements in service availability”, after millions of customers around the world suffered disruption Tell us: have you been affected by the Microsoft outage? Microsoft struggles to fix huge outage affecting Outlook and Teams What happened and when will it be fixed?
author: Guardian Technology

title: US denies IRGC destroyed American radar in Bahrain after southern Iran attack
content: The United States says the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps did not destroy an American radar in Bahrain following an attack on southern Iran. Despite rising military tensions, diplomatic efforts mediated by Qatar and Pakistan are continuing, and Tehran has said any resumption of formal negotiations with Washington will depend on its demands being met.
summary: The United States denied that the IRGC destroyed an American radar in Bahrain after an attack on southern Iran. Diplomatic efforts mediated by Qatar and Pakistan are continuing, with Tehran saying any resumption of formal negotiations with Washington depends on its demands being met.
author: Euronews

title: Dementia risk rises with daily cigarettes, 16% at 10 per day, 34% at 20
content: Researchers report that dementia risk rises with daily cigarette consumption. Compared with never‑smokers, individuals who smoke ten cigarettes per day have a 16 % higher risk, while those who smoke twenty per day face a 34 % higher risk. The increase is proportional to the number of cigarettes smoked.
summary: Researchers found that dementia risk increases with the number of cigarettes smoked per day. The risk rises by 16% for those who smoke 10 a day and by 34% for those who smoke 20, compared with people who have never smoked.
author: Euronews

title: Russian drone attacks kill two in Odesa, injure patients at Kyiv hospital
content: Russian overnight attacks in Ukraine killed at least two people in Odesa and injured another at a hospital in Kyiv. Rescuers evacuated patients, including those using wheelchairs and crutches, while firefighters worked to extinguish the resulting flames. The strikes hit the Kyiv hospital and caused casualties in Odesa.
summary: Russian overnight attacks killed at least two people in Odesa and injured another at a hospital in Kyiv. Rescuers evacuated patients, including those using wheelchairs and crutches, while firefighters fought the flames.
author: Euronews

title: Greenpeace unveils six-metre plastic‑filled Trojan Horse in Antalya during COP31
content: A six‑metre Trojan Horse overflowing with plastic waste was installed in Antalya as part of a Greenpeace International protest during the COP31 climate summit. The installation, created with Danish artist Thomas Dambo, is intended to highlight the environmental impact of plastics.
summary: A giant Trojan Horse overflowing with plastic waste appeared in Antalya as Greenpeace International staged a protest during the COP31 climate summit. The installation was created with Danish artist Thomas Dambo and warns of the environmental impact of plastics.
author: Euronews

title: Kriva Palanka asks government to declare 30‑day crisis over 1,000 roaming cows
content: More than 1,000 cows are roaming freely through Kriva Palanka in North Macedonia, damaging property and alarming residents. The town’s mayor has asked the government to declare a 30‑day state of crisis in response to the situation.
summary: More than 1,000 cows are roaming freely through Kriva Palanka in North Macedonia, damaging property and alarming residents. The mayor wants the government to declare a 30‑day state of crisis.
author: Euronews

title: Kew Gardens launches Christmas 2026 light trail with over a million lights
content: London’s Kew Gardens has launched its Christmas at Kew 2026 celebration, unveiling a light trail that incorporates more than a million lights across 24 installations. The display is anchored by a new fountain and a laser show that serve as the centerpiece of the event.
summary: London's Kew Gardens has unveiled a Christmas light trail featuring more than a million lights and 24 installations. The display includes a new fountain and a laser show as centrepieces.
author: Euronews

title: Four female students killed in Morelos as Mexico's femicide rate stays among highest
content: Mexico’s first female president, Claudia Sheinbaum, took office in 2024 and pledged to address violence against women. While national femicide figures have declined since her inauguration, the country still records roughly 520 murders of women this year. In the state of Morelos, located just outside Mexico City, four female students have been killed since January, one of them a Spanish exchange student. Morelos is reported as having one of the highest femicide rates in Mexico, highlighting ongoing impunity in the region.
summary: Since Claudia Sheinbaum became Mexico's first female president in 2024, femicides have fallen but remain high at about 520 murders this year. In the state of Morelos, four female students, including a Spanish exchange student, have been murdered since January, and the state has one of the country's highest femicide rates.
author: France 24

title: Russell Brand jailed over 10 years for rape, David Walliams accused of sexual misconduct
content: The United Kingdom is confronting a reckoning in entertainment after two prominent comedy figures became the focus of serious allegations. Russell Brand has been sentenced to more than ten years in prison after a conviction for rape and sexual assault, while David Walliams is currently facing serious allegations of sexual misconduct.
summary: Russell Brand was sentenced to more than 10 years in prison after being found guilty of rape and sexual assault. David Walliams is facing serious allegations of sexual misconduct.
author: France 24

title: Paris marks 11 years since 2015 terror attacks, emotions run high at Bataclan
content: France marked the 11th anniversary of the November 13, 2015 terror attacks that killed more than 130 people in Paris. Reporting from outside the Bataclan concert hall, one of the attack sites, France 24’s James André said the scene was marked by “a lot of emotion” as homage was paid to the victims.
summary: France marked 11 years since the November 13, 2015 terror attacks that left more than 130 dead in Paris. Outside the Bataclan concert venue, France 24's James André said there was a lot of emotion as homage was paid to the victims.
author: France 24

title: Most Ukrainians believe peace deal with Russia is impossible, says France 24
content:
Ukrainian attacks overnight killed at least nine people in Russia, while Russian forces struck a hospital in Kyiv and killed at least three people in the southern part of the country, officials on both sides said on Friday. The incidents were reported a day after intense shuttle diplomacy in U.S.-led talks aimed at ending the war, which is approaching its fifth year.

France 24’s Kyiv correspondent Gulliver Cragg said most people in Ukraine believe there is “no chance” of a peace deal being reached.
summary: Ukrainian attacks killed at least nine people in Russia overnight, and Moscow struck a hospital in Kyiv, killing at least three in the south, officials said Friday. France 24's correspondent in Kyiv Gulliver Cragg said most Ukrainians think there is no chance of a peace deal with Russia.
author: France 24

title: FRANCE 24’s Scoop examines US “Blue Tsunami” midterm impact on media
content: This week, FRANCE 24's media show Scoop looks at the impact of the midterm elections in the United States. While the results are being reckoned with by Republicans and celebrated by Democrats, what does it all mean for the press? Some media analysts wonder whether certain outlets, particularly ones accused of being cosy with the Trump administration, will change their tone. Our guest this week is International Affairs Commentator Douglas Herbert.
summary: FRANCE 24’s Scoop examines US “Blue Tsunami” midterm impact on media.
author: France 24

title: Syria covered up 2018 Douma chemical attack, France 24 reports
content:
On April 7 2018, a chemical attack struck the Syrian town of Douma, located on the outskirts of Damascus. According to the report, evidence initially pointed to the Syrian regime, but the proof later disappeared and eyewitnesses stopped speaking.

Eight years after the incident, France 24 journalist Jenna Le Bras located survivors and witnesses of the attack. She also interviewed representatives of several major institutions to examine how the regime, with Russian support, allegedly organized a large‑scale cover‑up of the incident.
summary: Syria covered up 2018 Douma chemical attack, France 24 reports.
author: France 24

title: Haitian security forces reclaim main stadium from gangs, Salvadoran soldiers guard
content:
Haitian security forces said they have regained control of the country’s main stadium, wresting it back from gangs that have been using it for the past two years. The operation was assisted by the Task Force, a private security group serving the government.

The stadium is now under the guard of Salvadoran soldiers. FRANCE 24 senior reporter Catherine Norris Trent described the area as a “devastated wasteland” and said retaking the stadium would be a significant step.
summary: Haitian security forces regained control of the country's main stadium from gangs that had occupied it for two years. The stadium is now guarded by Salvadoran soldiers with assistance from the Task Force private security group.
author: France 24

title: Roger Waters releases Arabic Comfortably Numb to aid Gaza, calls for genocide end
content: Pink Floyd co-founder Roger Waters has always mixed art with activism. A long-standing supporter of the Palestinian cause, the star guitarist has now released a re-imagined version of the rock anthem "Comfortably Numb" with Palestinian American singer Mona Miari singing in Arabic. He tells FRANCE 24's Lyana Saleh why proceeds of the record are going to the Palestine Children's Relief Fund and why he can never become "Comfortably Numb" with the violence and suffering in Gaza.
summary: Roger Waters releases Arabic Comfortably Numb to aid Gaza, calls for genocide end.
author: France 24

title: Jensen Huang steps down as Nvidia CEO amid extramarital affairs
content: Jensen Huang, who built Nvidia into the world’s dominant AI chipmaker, is stepping down as CEO over extramarital affairs. DW examines how losing its figurehead will affect the firm and the US‑China AI race.
summary: Jensen Huang, who built Nvidia into the world’s dominant AI chipmaker, is stepping down as CEO over extramarital affairs. DW examines how his departure could affect Nvidia and the US‑China AI race.
author: DW World

title: ANC grapples with worst local election result
content:
The ANC has suffered its worst local election result, leaving the party searching for answers.  
Experts attribute the outcome to public frustration with service delivery failures, indicating a political shift.
summary: The ruling ANC is searching for answers after a crushing local election result. Experts say the vote reflects public frustration with service delivery failures, signaling a political shift.
author: DW World

title: Czechia Prepares for Massive Protest Over Public Media Funding Cuts
content: Czechia is preparing for a massive protest in Prague on Sunday after a fast‑tracked bill to cut public‑media funding sparked strikes, rallies and concerns about the independence of public broadcasting. The planned demonstration reflects growing opposition to the proposed cuts.
summary: A fast‑tracked bill to cut public media funding has triggered strikes and rallies in Czechia. A massive protest is scheduled for Prague on Sunday.
author: DW World

title: Gaza's Humanitarian Crisis Worsens as Heavy Rain Damages Tents Amid Political Deadlock
content:
In war‑battered Gaza, heavy rain has flooded and damaged thousands of tents, and several people have died, worsening the humanitarian situation. The worsening conditions occur amid a political deadlock, with stalled peace talks.

A question is raised about whether pressure from “Trump’s Board of Peace” on Israel and Hamas could help ease the humanitarian crisis.
summary: Heavy rain in Gaza flooded and damaged thousands of tents, killing several people. Trump's Board of Peace is being asked to pressure Israel and Hamas to ease the humanitarian crisis amid stalled peace talks.
author: DW World

title: Tech stock sell‑off after US midterms raises doubts on Anthropic IPO
content: A sharp sell‑off in technology stocks following the U.S. midterm elections has raised questions about Anthropic’s pending initial public offering. Nonetheless, investors continue to commit hundreds of billions of dollars to artificial‑intelligence ventures, and some observers believe the AI sector remains robust.
summary: The sharp sell‑off in tech stocks after the US midterms has cast doubt on Anthropic’s looming IPO. Yet hundreds of billions are still being invested in AI, and some say the AI party is still in full swing.
author: DW World

title: Senior Indonesian police accused of illegally wiretapping President Prabowo Subianto
content: Senior police officers are accused of illegally monitoring President Prabowo Subianto. The scandal exposes rival networks within Indonesia’s security establishment and renews concerns about political misuse of surveillance.
summary: Senior police officers are accused of illegally monitoring President Prabowo Subianto. The allegations expose rival networks within Indonesia's security establishment and renewing concerns about political misuse of surveillance.
author: DW World

title: UN report says over 1,000 killed in Haiti July‑September as gangs terrorize
content:
A recent United Nations human‑rights report states that more than 1,000 people were killed in Haiti during the third quarter of the year.  

The report attributes the deaths to armed gangs that continue to terrorize residents in Port‑au‑Prince and other parts of the country.
summary: UN report says over 1,000 killed in Haiti July‑September as gangs terrorize.
author: UN News

title: Kenya starts 42‑day countdown to end Ebola after last patient discharged
content: Kenya launched a 42‑day countdown on Thursday to mark the end of its Ebola outbreak. The countdown began a day after the final patient under treatment was discharged and 11 individuals were released from quarantine.
summary: Kenya began a 42‑day countdown on Thursday to end its Ebola outbreak. The countdown started a day after the last patient was discharged and 11 people were released from quarantine.
author: UN News

title: COP31 focuses on cities and vulnerable communities as activists demand more action
content: At COP31 on Thursday, the human cost of climate change—illustrated by flooded homes and melting Himalayan glaciers—was highlighted. World leaders turned their focus to protecting cities and vulnerable communities, while activists pressed governments for greater action, underscoring the rising prominence of urban issues on the climate agenda.
summary: The human cost of climate change, shown by flooded homes and melting Himalayan glaciers, was highlighted at COP31 on Thursday. World leaders emphasized protecting cities and vulnerable communities while activists pressed governments for greater action.
author: UN News

title: UN agencies launch platform at COP31 to mobilize $3 billion for climate risk financing
content: UN agencies launched a joint platform at COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye, on Thursday. The initiative seeks to mobilise more than $3 billion in risk‑financing by 2030, with the goal of protecting 75 million people and their livelihoods from climate‑related shocks and natural hazards.
summary: UN agencies launched a joint platform at COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye on Thursday. The platform aims to secure access to more than $3 billion in risk financing to protect 75 million people and their livelihoods from climate shocks and natural hazards by 2030.
author: UN News

title: WFP chief says aid is only hope for millions in Sudan as funding cuts worsen hunger
content: The World Food Programme’s newly appointed Executive Director warned that funding cuts are deepening the hunger crisis in Sudan after his first field mission, during which he met families displaced by conflict who are struggling to feed their children. He said aid is the only hope for millions of Sudanese facing starvation.
summary: The World Food Programme’s new Executive Director warned that funding cuts are worsening Sudan’s hunger crisis. He issued the warning after his first field mission to Sudan, where he met families displaced by conflict and struggling to feed their children.
author: UN News

title: Ebola outbreak in DRC spreads as armed groups attack civilians and health workers
content: UN responders said on Friday that the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo continues to spread while repeated, ongoing deadly attacks on civilians and frontline health workers by armed groups are obstructing efforts to halt transmission, with the unrest fueled by those groups holding back the response.
summary: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo continues to spread. UN responders said on Friday that armed groups are repeatedly carrying out deadly attacks on civilians and frontline health workers, obstructing efforts to stop transmission.
author: UN News

title: COP31 launches guidance for credible AI-generated climate information
content: COP31 introduced a new initiative that issues guidance aimed at helping people worldwide obtain credible climate‑change information generated by artificial intelligence. The guidance also seeks to improve understanding of how AI technology affects the environment.
summary: New guidance has been issued to ensure people everywhere can obtain credible climate change information from artificial intelligence. The guidance also aims to help people understand how the technology impacts the environment.
author: UN News

title: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas says Russia setting traps in Ukraine talks
content: Kaja Kallas says Moscow is trying to divert attention from its aggression by raising issue of European security Europe live – latest updates The EU’s foreign policy chief has warned against “walking into the traps that Russia is setting” as she said Moscow was trying to start a debate about European security in order to divert attention from its aggression. “We have one aggressor and one victim, and the aggressor does not have security concerns,” Kaja Kallas said on arrival at an EU leaders’ summit in Dublin. “Nobody has ever attacked them. They have attacked others. I mean, keep the focus, people.”
summary: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas warned that Moscow is trying to divert attention from its aggression by raising European security issues. She said there is one aggressor and one victim, and the aggressor does not have security concerns, urging focus at the EU leaders’ summit in Dublin.
author: Guardian World

title: Ireland's secret banned books room opens to public after nearly a century
content: For nearly a century an Irish government building on St Stephen’s Green in Dublin housed a secret “banned books” room. The Department of Justice kept the collection, which holds about 12,000 volumes, closed to the public because the titles were deemed indecent or obscene. The censored works, dating from 1926 to 1996, were removed for themes “likely to corrupt or deprave” or for references to contraception or violence. According to the headline, the once‑hidden books have now been made publicly visible.
summary: A secret “banned books” room in the Department of Justice on St Stephen’s Green in Dublin held about 12,000 books censored between 1926 and 1996 for themes deemed likely to corrupt or deprave, or for references to contraception or violence. After almost a century of restricted access, the collection has been made publicly available.
author: Guardian World

title: EU chief Kaja Kallas warns Europe not to fall into Russia's Ukraine talk traps
content: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas warned Europe not to walk into Russia’s “traps” by agreeing to Moscow’s proposed sequence of events for Ukraine talks. Hungary’s Péter Magyar was also present, described as looking very elegant, and reportedly took a brief detour on his way back to his hotel to pour a perfect pint of Guinness.
summary: EU chief Kaja Kallas warns Europe not to fall into Russia's Ukraine talk traps.
author: Guardian World

title: Victorian Greens refuse preferences to Labor in 15 seats, sparking accusations of “dodgy deals”
content:
The Greens have announced that they will not direct preferences to Labor in 15 Victorian electorates after Labor’s decision earlier this week to run an open ticket in a key inner‑city seat. The Greens describe Labor’s move as “unforgivable” and say the preference refusal is a retaliation.

The dispute has escalated into a war of words, with both parties accusing each other of striking a “dodgy deal” that could benefit the Liberal Party and One Nation in the election scheduled for 28 November.
summary: The Greens said they will not direct preferences to Labor in 15 Victorian electorates after Labor ran an open ticket in a key inner‑city seat. Both parties have accused each other of a “dodgy deal” that could help the Liberals and One Nation in the election on 28 November.
author: Guardian World

title: A baffling trail from Australia to Singapore: what is Megaspeed, the company implicated in downfall of Nvidia’s Jensen Huang?
content:
Megaspeed International is a cloud‑computing firm that is registered in Singapore and lists affiliates in the United States, Asia and Australia. According to the report, its physical presence includes a lottery retailer in rural Australia, a dilapidated storefront in Kuala Lumpur and a near‑empty office in Singapore, creating a “puzzling corporate picture.”  

The company has been linked to the downfall of Nvidia chief Jensen Huang, and its former director, Alice Huang, has been accused of being a Chinese spy. Employees at the various locations say they know nothing about the cloud‑computing business that is at the centre of a global spy scandal.
summary: A baffling trail from Australia to Singapore: what is Megaspeed, the company implicated in downfall of Nvidia’s Jensen Huang?
author: Guardian World

title: Former NSW Liberal MP Rory Amon convicted of raping 13-year-old boy
content:
Former NSW Liberal MP Rory Amon, 37, has been found guilty of raping a 13-year-old boy. A jury at the state’s supreme court convicted him of one count of sexual intercourse with a person aged between 10 and 14 and indecently assaulting a child. The verdict was reached after approximately four hours of deliberation on Friday.

This conviction follows a previous trial where a different jury failed to reach a verdict on the same charges. The former politician now faces the possibility of a significant jail term.
summary: A jury in the New South Wales Supreme Court found former Liberal MP Rory Amon guilty of one count of sexual intercourse with a person aged 10 to 14 and indecent assault of a child. Amon, 37, was convicted after about four hours of deliberation and faces a significant jail term.
author: Guardian World

title: Howard Lutnick faces possible removal over inaction in Nvidia spying scandal
content:
US commerce secretary Howard Lutnick is reported to be facing possible dismissal as criticism mounts over his alleged inaction in the Nvidia spying scandal. Warnings have emerged about an alleged Chinese spy’s connections to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and about delays in adding the entity Megaspeed to a trade blacklist, prompting calls for Lutnick’s removal.

Jensen Huang resigned from Nvidia on Thursday and was succeeded on an interim basis by chief financial officer Colette Kress. Reports accompanying his departure cite multiple affairs, most prominently with Alice Huang, who is suspected of being a Chinese spy.
summary: US commerce secretary faces sack as warnings emerge about alleged Chinese spy’s ties to Jensen Huang and delays in adding Megaspeed to trade blacklist Analysis: Jensen Huang built an AI kingdom. Now he’s gone, will Nvidia’s ramparts be breached?
author: Guardian World

title: Storm Charles triggers floods and flight cancellations across southern Europe
content:
Storm Charles has produced heavy rain and strong south‑westerly winds across the Iberian Peninsula, beginning on the Portuguese island of Madeira before reaching the mainland on 11 November. At Funchal airport a wind gust of 84.5 mph (136 km/h) was recorded and rainfall totals hit 355 mm (13.97 in) in a 12‑hour period.

The storm’s impact on air travel was marked by 183 flight cancellations at Lisbon’s airport on Wednesday—about one‑third of its normal daily traffic—and 155 cancellations at Madrid‑Barajas airport. After flooding in Spain and Portugal, the system moved north‑eastward through southern France, causing significant flooding in Cannes, rock falls and road closures along the French Riviera.

In Italy, the weather service issued a red rainfall warning, its highest level, for the region from Tuscany to Venezia. Forecast models predict an additional 100 mm of rain across Italy and the Balkans in the coming days, with up to 200 mm possible in mountainous areas.
summary: Storm Charles triggers floods and flight cancellations across southern Europe.
author: Guardian World

title: Robertson pays tribute to Dalglish as he matches Scotland cap record
content:
Tottenham full-back Andy Robertson will match Kenny Dalglish’s Scotland cap record of 102 appearances during Friday’s match against North Macedonia at Hampden Park. Robertson stated that achieving this milestone does not equate to reputational parity with Dalglish, who is widely regarded as the country’s finest player and ended his international career with the same tally four decades ago.

The defender expressed delight at reaching the figure, noting he is expected to surpass the record in Switzerland on Monday. Robertson paid tribute to Dalglish, whom he came to know well during their nine years together at Liverpool, describing the achievement as another reason to honor one of the greatest players.
summary: Robertson pays tribute to Dalglish as he matches Scotland cap record.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Morgan Rogers says claims Cole Palmer does not want to play for England are a lie
content: Forward springs to defence of Chelsea teammate ‘He wanted to come and represent his country’ Morgan Rogers has said accusations that his Chelsea teammate Cole Palmer is not committed to playing for England are “a lie”. Palmer, who was left out of the squad for this week’s Nations League ties against Croatia and Spain, has faced questions over his desire to play international football since withdrawing from last month’s camp with a groin injury. Thomas Tuchel, who did not take the 24-year-old to last summer’s World Cup, expressed irritation at the time, saying the Chelsea attacker “misses too many opportunities” to play for his country.
summary: Morgan Rogers stated that accusations his Chelsea teammate Cole Palmer lacks commitment to playing for England are false. Rogers defended Palmer, who was omitted from the squad for upcoming Nations League matches, by asserting that his teammate wanted to represent his country.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Italy beat France 3-1 as Esposito's brace ends Zidane's unbeaten run
content:
Italy defeated France 3-1 at San Siro to take the top spot in their Nations League group, marking Zinedine Zidane’s first loss as France head coach. Michael Olise opened the scoring for the visitors after 10 minutes, capitalizing on an error by Gianluigi Donnarumma. Pio Esposito then struck twice, with Davide Frattesi also finding the net, as Italy mounted a comeback with goals either side of half-time.

In other Nations League action, Spain defeated Czechia 2-0 to maintain a 100% record.
summary: Pio Esposito scored twice to help Italy defeat France 3-1 at San Siro, securing the top spot in their Nations League group. This result marked the first defeat for Zinedine Zidane as France head coach, following an early goal by Michael Olise off a Gianluigi Donnarumma error.
author: Guardian Sport

title: USMNT faces uncertainty as Mauricio Pochettino nears Manchester United move
content: The USMNT head coach is on the verge of sealing a move to Manchester United, but it’s hard to know who could be in the chair next Sign up for our free newsletter here Even before the 2026 World Cup, the US Soccer Federation projected an air of confidence in its ability to, someday, replace Mauricio Pochettino. “We have a process of, on a regular basis, always reviewing sort of succession planning for all of our key roles at US Soccer,” JT Batson, the federation CEO, told ESPN in April. “We’re ready when anything happens, whether it’s CFO, whether it’s a head coach or anything in between.”
summary: USMNT head coach Mauricio Pochettino is on the verge of sealing a move to Manchester United, leaving the federation without a clear successor. US Soccer CEO JT Batson stated in April that the organization maintains a regular succession planning process for key roles and is ready if a head coach departs.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Commanders rally for 24-21 win over Giants with last‑minute Diggs TD
content:
The Washington Commanders defeated the New York Giants 24-21 on Thursday night in a must-win game for Washington. Jayden Daniels threw his third touchdown pass of the game, a 32-yarder to Stefon Diggs with 57 seconds remaining, to seal the victory. The decisive play came after Daniels threw his first two interceptions of the season to end the previous two drives.

Daniels finished the game 23 of 33 for 249 yards. In addition to the game-winning pass to Diggs, he recorded touchdown throws to Ben Sinnott and Antonio Williams.
summary: Washington defeated the New York Giants 24‑21 on Thursday night after Jayden Daniels connected with Stefon Diggs on a 32‑yard touchdown pass with 57 seconds remaining. Daniels finished 23 of 33 for 249 yards and also threw touchdown passes to Ben Sinnott and Antonio Williams after earlier throwing two interceptions.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Harry Kane wins Ballon d’Or and scores on record 126th England appearance
content:
Harry Kane marked his 126th appearance for England by scoring a goal, extending his record-breaking run for the national team. The achievement came shortly after Kane received the Ballon d’Or, an award that validated his career. The article, written by Barney Ronay, describes the event as a celebratory occasion characterized by extensive media attention and tributes leading up to the match.

The piece highlights the overwhelming focus on Kane during the period, noting a week filled with montages and tributes. The author employs the concept of semantic satiation to illustrate how the repetition of Kane’s name and achievements in the buildup to the game rendered the term almost meaningless. The article portrays the night as a unique event where Kane’s presence and contributions were the central focus, culminating in his goal during the final match of the cycle.
summary: Harry Kane won the Ballon d’Or and scored a goal during his record-breaking 126th appearance for England. The article describes the event as the climax of a week filled with tributes and montages celebrating the forward.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Australia Test captain Pat Cummins calls Khawaja's sandpaper claims “complete and utter nonsense”
content: Cummins insists he did not know of ball-tampering plot in South Africa ‘No masterplan around using illegal methods,’ Cummins says ‘Abrasive’, ‘arrogant’ and ‘ugly’: standout moments from the press conference Pat Cummins flatly denied Usman Khawaja’s claims that the entire Australian cricket team was implicated in the 2018 sandpaper scandal, saying at a press conference in Sydney the allegations were “complete and utter nonsense”and “100% wrong”. The Test captain’s defiant appearance on Friday morning prompted David Warner to later accuse Cummins of throwing Khawaja under the bus as the feud engulfing Australian cricket continued.
summary: Pat Cummins denied Usman Khawaja's allegations that the Australian cricket team was involved in the 2018 sandpaper scandal, calling them “complete and utter nonsense” and “100% wrong” at a press conference in Sydney. David Warner later accused Cummins of throwing Khawaja under the bus.
author: Guardian Sport

title: BBC Sport reviews six key matches from Carrick's Man Utd tenure
content: BBC Sport has published a retrospective examining six Premier League matches that marked the highs and lows of Michael Carrick’s 10-month tenure as Manchester United manager.
summary: BBC Sport examines six Premier League matches that defined the highs and lows of Michael Carrick's time at Manchester United. The review covers his 10-month spell in charge of the club.

title: Arsenal draw 1-1 with Barcelona to extend unbeaten start
content: Arsenal secured a 1-1 draw against Barcelona at the Camp Nou, extending their unbeaten start in the Uefa Women's Champions League to four matches. The point moves Renee Slegers' team into the top four, positioning them well to automatically qualify for the knockout stages.
summary: Arsenal held Barcelona to a 1-1 draw at the Camp Nou to extend their unbeaten start to four matches in the Uefa Women's Champions League. The point moves Renee Slegers' side into the top four, placing them in a strong position to qualify for the knockout stages.
author: BBC Sport

title: US Army officer involved in alleged Russian spying scheme identified: Reports
content: The U. S. Army officer arrested in the United Kingdom this week for alleged involvement in a Russian espionage scheme has been identified as Lt. Col. Brandon Tyner. The 41‑year‑old soldier was detained on Tuesday following a sting operation and is expected to be charged in the U. K. early next week.
summary: US Army officer involved in alleged Russian spying scheme identified: Reports.

Smith in an interview at the White House. “I had…

title: Boebert blames policy, corruption, ‘markets’ for possible loss
content: Incumbent Rep. Lauren Boebert (R) attributed her potential loss in Colorado’s 4th Congressional District to policy, corruption, and “markets” on Thursday. She made these remarks to NewsNation’s Blake Burman while noting the presence of various variables in the race. The contest remains too close to call more than a week before Election Day.
summary: Incumbent Rep. Lauren Boebert (R) blamed her potential loss in Colorado’s 4th Congressional District on policy, corruption and “markets” Thursday as her race remains too close to call more than a week out from Election Day.

title: Van Hollen says he will challenge Schumer for majority leader
content: Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.) announced on Thursday that he will challenge Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N. Y.) for the position of majority leader. In a post on the social platform X, Van Hollen called for “new leadership” in the Senate, setting up a contest as Democrats prepare to retake the majority in the upper chamber.
