(Hours after Huang's resignation was announced, Reuters reported that he also had an "intimate relationship" with another Nvidia employee.) Prominent voices in technology have come out in support of Huang, w …
summary: Nvidia announced that Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO following reports of affairs involving an alleged Chinese spy and a direct report. Prominent voices in technology have come out in support of Huang following the announcement.
author: The Verge

title: Google launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen model for complex queries
content:
Google has introduced its new Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, which is designed to provide more helpful answers to complex inquiries. The model can handle questions with multiple parts, difficult typos, and highly specific requests by breaking them down and addressing each component individually.

The new model is available immediately across Search, the Gemini app, Google AI Studio, the Gemini API, Gemini for business, and Google Antigravity for AI Pro and Ultra subscribers. Robby Stein, VP of product at Google Search, stated that Gemini 4 Hydrogen is now the default model in AI Mode and is used for difficult questions in AI Overviews.
summary: Google's new Gemini 4 Hydrogen model is designed to handle complex questions with multiple parts or typos by breaking them down for detailed responses. The model is now the default in AI Mode and is available across Google Search, the Gemini app, and various developer platforms.
author: The Verge

title: Microsoft Tests New Xbox Customization Options for Backgrounds and Guide Menu
content:
Microsoft has begun testing new customization options for Xbox consoles, initially available to Xbox Insiders. The updates include rotating backgrounds, enhanced library management for digital games, and the option to relocate the Xbox Guide menu to the right-hand side. Eden Marie, principal software engineering lead at Xbox, noted that users can now save favorite dynamic backgrounds and automatically shuffle through them.

The background settings allow users to select "Shuffle" at the start of any category, with options to change the background upon sign-in or on an hourly, daily, or weekly basis. These features are part of a broader effort to improve how players organize their disc-to-digital game libraries.
summary: Microsoft Tests New Xbox Customization Options for Backgrounds and Guide Menu.
author: The Verge

title: Microsoft Outlook Email Service Down Worldwide
content:
Microsoft Outlook has been experiencing widespread outages since just before 1 PM ET on Thursday, with users globally reporting an inability to access email via web or apps. Microsoft acknowledged the disruption through its Microsoft 365 Status account, attributing the connectivity errors to elevated load affecting a portion of its infrastructure across multiple regions.

While the primary issue affects Outlook, some users also reported problems with Teams, though to a lesser degree. Microsoft’s official updates indicated that customers might encounter issues across its broader suite of 365 business services. Microsoft communications director Ben Hope also addressed the situation.
summary: Microsoft Outlook email service is down worldwide as of just before 1PM ET on Thursday, affecting web and app access. Microsoft said a portion of infrastructure is under elevated load across multiple regions, causing connectivity errors, and customers may also experience issues with other 365 services.
author: The Verge

title: Humble Bundle redesign removes two-factor verification from settings
content:
Humble Bundle recently redesigned its storefront, but the new settings page no longer includes options to add or update two-factor verification methods, according to Kotaku. PC Gamer noted that while support pages still discuss two-factor verification, the feature is missing from the current interface, despite the publication’s writer having previously set it up on the old site.

Despite the removal of explicit settings, some form of two-factor verification appears to remain active. The article’s author reported being prompted to check their email for a code when attempting to log into their Humble Bundle account during the writing process.
summary: The new Humble Bundle storefront redesign removed the option to add or update two‑factor verification from the settings page. Despite support pages still discussing two‑factor verification and the writer having set it up on the old site, a form of two‑factor verification appears to remain active.
author: The Verge

title: Whoop launches Humans social network with verified heartbeats
content: Starting Thursday, Whoop members can share their data from its wearables on the app's new Whoop Humans social network. Users can make their metrics, activities, and achievements visible to other Whoop wearers, post Story-like "Moments" with photos and captions, and add comments and reactions on other members' posts. Whoop claims its platform is "entirely human," unlike other social media platforms that are "saturated with artificial intelligence, automated accounts and bots, and manufactured content." Whoop CEO Will Ahmed says Humans is "the most verifiably human network ever launched. Every account represents a real person with a verified …
summary: Whoop members can now share wearable data, activities, and achievements on its new social network. The platform features verified heartbeats to ensure every account represents a real person.
author: The Verge

title: Google Faces Calls for AI Moratoriums in Schools After Gemini Pilot Backlash
content: CHICAGO—Families joined protests in seven cities nationwide on Wednesday, rallying against what they see as Google’s bid to entrench its AI models in schools, turn kids of all ages into Gemini guinea pigs, and hook them on AI. The backlash follows a Google statement last week, confirming that there will be no way for students to use Google Search without AI. While Google claimed it was giving schools “more choice, not less”—by turning off Search, Gemini, and Gemini Notebook by default—it would not provide an option that allowed Search without AI. For students, the only way to avoid interacting with AI was to remember to add “-ai” to every query, parents worried. In Chicago, many families showed up to protest Google, despite cold, rainy weather. Waving signs, dozens of protesters marched up to Google’s downtown office as workers seemed to be leaving for the day, shouting chants like “Hey Google, nice try, we don’t want your Gemini” and “Hey, Google, leave our kids alone!” Read full article Comments
summary: Families protested in seven cities nationwide on Wednesday against Google's plan to embed its Gemini AI models in schools. Google confirmed last week that students will not be able to use Google Search without AI, despite claiming it was providing more choice.
author: Ars Technica

title: Google launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen, replacing Gemini 3.8 Flash
content: Google is continuing its elemental AI naming scheme with the new Gemini 4 Hydrogen. These names are less descriptive than the Pro/Flash monikers of earlier releases, but Hydrogen's purpose is clear: It replaces the faster, more economical Flash models most people in Google's ecosystem use. With Google's recent Argon and Carbon releases, the rollout was staged and began with cybersecurity researchers. Even when general availability began, Google restricted access to users paying for its most expensive AI subscription. The limits for Hydrogen are much more relaxed, with access beginning immediately. This model has replaced Gemini 3.8 Flash across the company's products. Google claims that Hydrogen represents a major improvement versus the previous Flash model. It runs in one of four thinking levels (low, medium, high, and the new xhigh), and even in high mode, it's 2.5 times faster than Flash 3.8. Plus, it reduces "fabricated claims" by more than 5x, according to Google's analysis. Users will also see gains in code generation, with Hydrogen more than tripling 3.8 Flash's score in Terminal-Bench. In some cases, Hydrogen even trades blows with Argon. It managed a score of 54 in the popular Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index with xhigh mode versus 50 for Argon. Read full article Comments
summary: Google is continuing its elemental AI naming scheme with the new Gemini 4 Hydrogen. These names are less descriptive than the Pro/Flash monikers of earlier releases, but Hydrogen's purpose is clear: It replaces the faster, more economical Flash models most people in Google's ecosystem use.
author: Ars Technica

title: Elder Scrolls Travels: Shadowkey Receives 4K PC Remaster
content:
The Elder Scrolls franchise is adding a long‑forgotten title to its catalog: The Elder Scrolls Travels: Shadowkey is receiving a 4K PC remake. The original game launched in 2004 for the Nokia N‑Gage, a handheld console that offered 176 × 208 pixel resolution and hack‑and‑slash RPG combat.

Shadowkey was one of the few mobile entries in the series, and its low‑resolution graphics and fast‑paced gameplay set it apart from the console and PC releases that followed. The upcoming 4K update will bring the title to modern PC hardware, offering a high‑definition visual experience while preserving the core gameplay that defined the original.
summary: Elder Scrolls Travels: Shadowkey, a 2004 Nokia N‑Gage mobile hack‑and‑slash RPG, is being remastered for PC in 4K resolution. The original game featured 176×208 pixel resolution and is considered one of the franchise's most obscure titles.
author: Ars Technica

title: Drone Attacks on Data Centers Raise Big Tech Security Concerns
content:
Drone and missile strikes have inflicted unprecedented damage on data centers in Eastern Europe and the Middle East this year, disrupting cloud services for millions of people and permanently deleting some Amazon Web Services customer data. This trend has raised new concerns for Big Tech companies, governments, and anyone who relies on common digital services in modern life.

To examine what these attacks mean for society’s reliance on cloud resilience, Ars Live will host a live conversation titled “Drone attacks and data centers: New Risks for Big Tech” on Tuesday, November 17 at 1 pm ET with Joseph Jarnecki.

Joseph Jarnecki is a senior research fellow at the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI), a UK defense and security think tank. He leads RUSI’s work on how cloud services factor into national security and defense, along with tech sovereignty efforts. Jarnecki has researched how Ukraine strengthened its cloud resilience with Western partners despite facing both cyberattacks and kinetic attacks at the start of the full‑scale Russian invasion, and has explored the implications for NATO and European governments’ cloud adoption plans.
summary: Drone Attacks on Data Centers Raise Big Tech Security Concerns.
author: Ars Technica

title: FAA expands AI tool to manage air traffic across US airspace
content:
The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has announced that it will extend the use of its AI‑driven advisory system, SMART, to all 22 air traffic control centers across the United States. The expansion follows a successful initial deployment in the National Capital Region that began on September 21.

The $875 million SMART system has already rerouted 180 flights in the Washington, DC, airspace. According to FAA data, the system has saved an average of 10 minutes per flight and nearly 80 gallons of fuel per flight. The agency hopes the same efficiencies can be achieved nationwide.

Airline executives have expressed support for the rollout. In contrast, the labor union that represents air traffic controllers stated that it was not involved in designing or testing the AI‑driven system.

In a statement posted on November 10, the FAA said, “After a successful initial rollout to the National Capital Region in September, the FAA will now use SMART in the airspace of all 22 centers across the country to reduce delays, reduce fuel consumption and improve the travel experience for the flying public.”
summary: The FAA has expanded the $875 million SMART AI system to advise air traffic controllers across all 22 national airspace centers after a successful rollout in the National Capital Region. Airline executives support the rollout, but the air traffic controllers' union said it was not involved in designing or testing the system.
author: Ars Technica

title: American Cancer Society Recommends Routine PSA Screening for All Men
content:
The American Cancer Society has revised its prostate‑cancer screening guidelines, now urging routine PSA testing for all men. The update was released Thursday and marks a shift from previous recommendations that limited routine screening to certain age groups.

Under the new rules, men at average risk should receive a PSA test every two years between ages 50 and 69. Men identified as high risk because of race or family history are advised to begin testing earlier, at age 45, and to have the test annually.

All Black men are specifically recommended to start yearly PSA testing at age 45. Non‑Black men who have a close relative diagnosed with prostate cancer before age 65, or who have more than one relative with the disease, should also begin yearly testing at 45. If a non‑Black man has only one close relative diagnosed at age 65 or older, he should start PSA screening at 45 but can have the test every two years.
summary: In a significant update to its guidelines for prostate cancer screening, the American Cancer Society is now recommending that all men get routinely screened for prostate cancer with a PSA test. Men at average risk should get a PSA test every two years from age 50 to 69, according to the new guidelines released Thursday.
author: Ars Technica

title: Nebius Plans $40 Billion AI Expansion Funded by Prepayments and Loans
content:
Nebius is testing the neocloud playbook by planning a $40 billion AI infrastructure expansion. The company intends to fund this spend through customer prepayments and loans.  

However, delays at a Microsoft data center have raised questions about Nebius’s financing model.
summary: Nebius plans to fund its $40 billion AI infrastructure expansion through customer prepayments and loans. Delays at a Microsoft data center have raised questions about its financing model.
author: TechCrunch

content: Jensen Huang has resigned from Nvidia after an affair. The resignation is noted as potentially affecting national security amid the United States and China’s competition to build the most advanced AI infrastructure.
summary: Jensen Huang has resigned from Nvidia following an affair, which could have ramifications for national security as the U. S.

title: Democrats launch second Nvidia probe, letter criticizes Huang's scheme with Trump
content: Democrats have launched a second Congressional investigation into Nvidia’s sales to China and its dealings with former President Trump, following the emergence of the alleged spy affair. The inquiry is accompanied by a scathing letter that accuses Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang of orchestrating a scheme involving Trump.
summary: This is the second Congressional investigation into Nvidia's China sales and its dealings with Trump since the alleged spy affair broke. Democrats have launched the investigation and written a scathing letter about Huang’s scheme with Trump.
author: TechCrunch

title: Jensen Huang's affair turns him into political liability for Nvidia
content: CEO was viewed as ‘irreplaceable’, but recklessness of affair with a woman regarded by US officials as a Chinese spy made him a political liability Half the tech world made up its mind before the facts could be assessed properly. Jensen Huang was “irreplaceable”, said the chorus at the start of this week. Nvidia would melt without the co-founder’s brilliance, apparently. The chipmaker’s board had to find a way to save its genius for the sake of corporate America and the entire AI universe. It was always nonsense because, after the passage of only a few days since his confession of infidelity, Huang looked less like a towering corporate titan and more like a political liability.
summary: CEO was viewed as ‘irreplaceable’, but recklessness of affair with a woman regarded by US officials as a Chinese spy made him a political liability Half the tech world made up its mind before the facts could be assessed properly. Jensen Huang was “irreplaceable”, said the chorus at the start of this week.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Drones Deliver Food to Chimpanzees at Flooded Fort Pierce Sanctuary
content:
Flooding at a chimpanzee sanctuary in Fort Pierce, Florida, has made it difficult for staff to reach some of the animals.  

To keep the chimpanzees fed, workers are using drones to deliver food—including bananas—while large portions of the property remain underwater.
summary: Flooding at a chimpanzee sanctuary in Fort Pierce, Florida, has made it difficult for staff to reach some of the animals. Workers are using drones to deliver food, including bananas, while large parts of the property remain underwater.
author: Euronews

title: Russian officer killed by car bomb in St Petersburg, murder probe opened
content:
A Russian officer was killed by a car bomb in St Petersburg, and a murder investigation has begun.  

Kyiv rarely claims responsibility for such attacks on Russian troops, but Ukrainian forces have previously used similar blasts to show that Russia’s security services are vulnerable.
summary: A Russian officer was killed by a car bomb in St Petersburg and a murder investigation has begun. Ukrainian forces have previously used similar blasts to show Russia’s security services are vulnerable, though Kyiv rarely claims responsibility for attacks on Russian troops.
author: Euronews

title: Doomsday study predicted world end on 13 November 2026
content: A study predicted that humanity would end on Friday, 13 November 2026. The prediction is now considered outdated, yet it remains a fascinating example of doomsday forecasting.
summary: A study predicted the world would end on 13 November 2026, but the study is now considered outdated. The prediction remains a point of fascination.
author: Euronews

title: Russia calls US Caspian task force illegal; study notes Tehran-Moscow sanction evasion
content: After CENTCOM affirmed it would maintain the naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz and block the IRGC’s land and Caspian routes, Russia called this special taskforce a 'clear violation of international law'. At the same time, the Institute for the Study of War devoted its latest assessment to Tehran-Moscow cooperation in circumventing US arms restrictions.
summary: Russia calls US Caspian task force illegal; study notes Tehran-Moscow sanction evasion.
author: Euronews

title: US New Congress Members Take Traditional Photo at Capitol Hill
content: Newly elected U.S. lawmakers assembled on Capitol Hill on Thursday, 12 November, for a traditional group photograph before the opening of the 120th Congress. The incoming House members are also attending orientation sessions following the November midterm elections.
summary: Newly elected US lawmakers gathered on Capitol Hill on Thursday 12 November for a traditional group photograph ahead of the opening of the 120th Congress. The incoming House members are attending orientation following the November midterm elections.
author: Euronews

title: Harvard brain injury expert says no contact sport is safe after teen rugby death
content:
FRANCE 24’s Mark Owen interviewed Dr Daniel H Daneshvar, Associate Professor at Harvard Medical School, about the dangers of contact sports and brain injury risk. The conversation was prompted by the recent death of a 17‑year‑old French woman who died last month after a head collision on a rugby field.

Daneshvar said there is no such thing as safe in contact sports. He explained that repeated head hits increase the risk of problems later in life, both in the near term and the long term.
summary: Harvard brain injury expert says no contact sport is safe after teen rugby death.
author: France 24

title: Amnesty International says UN failed to protect civilians in South Sudan massacre
content:
Amnesty International accuses the government and UN peacekeepers of failing to protect civilians during a massacre in South Sudan that killed over 200 people.  

In other news, more than a thousand people are prosecuted for illegal mining in Guinea. And a Malagasy king has finally returned home a century after French colonial troops killed him.
summary: Amnesty International accuses the South Sudanese government and UN peacekeepers of failing to protect civilians during a massacre that killed over 200 people. More than a thousand people face prosecution for illegal mining in Guinea, and a Malagasy king whose ancestors were killed by French colonial troops has been repatriated.
author: France 24

title: Tunisians among over 1,400 Africans recruited by Russia for Ukraine war
content: A new report says more than 1,400 Africans have been recruited to fight for Russia in Ukraine since 2023, including Tunisians. Meanwhile, South Africa is pursuing a role as Africa’s digital gateway, prompting a backlash in Cape Town, and Chad’s city of Abéché hosted an arts festival featuring music, dance and theatre that attracted many young spectators.
summary: A new report says more than 1,400 Africans have been recruited to fight for Russia in Ukraine since 2023, including Tunisians. The same briefing notes a backlash to South Africa’s digital‑gateway plans in Cape Town and an arts festival in Chad that attracted young audiences.
author: France 24

title: Satellite images show Mauritania fishing port, not migrant fleet bound for Spain
content:
Spain’s Canary Islands have declared a state of emergency as they confront renewed pressure from migrant arrivals. A viral video circulated online asserting that thousands of boats were gathering in Mauritania’s port, allegedly “ready to set sail” to transport migrants to the archipelago.

Satellite imagery examined in the video’s fact‑check shows the scene to be a traditional fishing port rather than a large migrant fleet. The analysis, presented by Vedika Bahl in the “Truth or Fake” segment, concludes that the video’s claim is misleading.
summary: Spain’s Canary Islands have declared a state of emergency amid renewed migrant arrivals. A viral video claimed thousands of Mauritanian boats were ready to sail migrants to the islands, but satellite images show only a traditional fishing port, as explained by Vedika Bahl in Truth or Fake.
author: France 24

title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO amid romantic scandal
content:
Jensen Huang has stepped down from his roles as Nvidia’s President, chief executive officer and board member, according to the report. The announcement follows romantic affairs that the source says erased hundreds of billions of dollars from the company’s market value within days.  

The same report notes that U.S. lawmakers indicate they will likely pursue tighter export restrictions on AI chips, and that the rapid expansion of AI data‑centre infrastructure is generating anger and concern among French communities.
summary: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia's President, CEO and board member, with his romantic affairs wiping hundreds of billions of dollars from the company's market value in days. US lawmakers signaled they may push for tighter export restrictions on AI chips, while the rapid AI data centre buildout is sparking anger and worries among French communities.
author: France 24

title: Expert says Russia uses illegal, unethical tactics, believing Europe won't reciprocate
content:
Elisabeth Braw, a Senior Fellow with the Atlantic Council’s Transatlantic Security Initiative, told FRANCE 24 that Russia aims to increase its power at the expense of European countries. She stated that the easiest method for this is to constantly wage a "dirty war" against Europe using illegal and unethical means. Braw noted that Russia employs these tactics because it knows European nations are not going to use the same means in return.

These comments address mounting concerns across Europe that recent hoax threats and cyber attacks may be part of a massive hybrid warfare campaign.
summary: Elisabeth Braw, Senior Fellow with the Atlantic Council’s Transatlantic Security Initiative, said Russia aims to increase its power at the expense of European countries by waging a dirty war using illegal and unethical means. She added that Russia knows Europe will not use the same means in response.
author: France 24

title: Eight killed, including two children, after Brooklyn residential building collapses
content: Eight people, including two children, died when a residential building in Brooklyn collapsed into a neighboring construction site on Wednesday. Firefighters spent hours searching the rubble overnight and declared the operation concluded on Thursday. Authorities have opened an investigation into the disaster.
summary: Eight people, including two children, were killed when a residential building in Brooklyn collapsed into an adjacent construction site on Wednesday. Firefighters searched the rubble overnight and ended the operation on Thursday as authorities opened an investigation.
author: France 24

title: Israel hits Gaza hospital, says Hamas senior figure was inside
content: Israel said it struck a Gaza hospital because a senior Hamas figure was inside and the site was being used as a military command center. Palestinian officials reported that the attack killed at least six people, including a surgeon. The strike took place while the ceasefire in the region remains increasingly fragile.
summary: Israel said Hamas was using the Gaza hospital as a military command center. Palestinian officials reported at least six people killed, including a surgeon, as the strike occurred amid an increasingly fragile ceasefire.
author: DW World

title: Czechia prepares for massive Prague protest on November 15 over media reform bill
content: Czechia is preparing for a massive protest in Prague on November 15 after a fast‑tracked bill on public‑media funding reform sparked strikes, rallies and concerns about the independence of public broadcasting. The legislation’s rapid passage has intensified public anger over the government’s proposed changes.
summary: A fast-tracked bill on public media funding reform has sparked strikes, rallies and fears for the independence of public broadcasting in Czechia. A massive protest is due to take place in Prague on November 15.
author: DW World

title: EU leaders debate who will represent Europe at Russia‑Ukraine peace talks
content: EU leaders are debating which European official should attend forthcoming peace talks with Russia on Ukraine. A U.S. envoy, after meeting President Putin, said that a European seat at the negotiating table now appears likely. The identity of the European representative, however, has not yet been determined.
summary: A seat at the table for Europe now appears likely after comments by a US envoy who just held talks with Putin. EU leaders are still unclear about which official will take that seat.
author: DW World

title: Angela Rayner approves planning permission for Piddington asylum centre
content: The communities secretary, Angela Rayner, has granted full planning permission for an asylum centre on a Ministry of Defence site near the Oxfordshire village of Piddington. The approval covers refurbishment and redevelopment of the former barracks and would accommodate 1,200 asylum seekers. The village, which voted to leave the United Kingdom, has opposed the proposal. The Home Office, however, must still give its sign‑off, and officials say final approval remains to be determined.
summary: Communities secretary Angela Rayner has approved full planning permission for an asylum centre at a Ministry of Defence site near the Oxfordshire village of Piddington. The Home Office says final approval for the site, which would house 1,200 asylum seekers, is still to be determined.
author: Guardian World

title: Israeli airstrike on Gaza's Nasser hospital kills surgeon, five others, wounds 28
content:
An Israeli airstrike on Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis, southern Gaza, killed six people and wounded 28, the hospital director reported. Among those killed was a surgeon and a disabled man. The hospital is one of the few remaining medical facilities in the strip.

The Israeli military carried out the attack early on Thursday. In a statement it said it had struck a Hamas commander and other fighters at the hospital, but it did not provide evidence to support that claim.
summary: An Israeli airstrike on Nasser hospital in Khan Younis killed six people, including a surgeon and a disabled man. The attack wounded 28 others, according to the hospital director, while the Israeli military said it targeted a Hamas commander and fighters.
author: Guardian World

title: NAZA documentary on Gaza now in cinemas worldwide, free online from early December
content: The Guardian’s Gaza documentary NAZA features testimony from 24 Israeli officials who were involved in surveillance and remote killing of Palestinian civilians. The film is currently playing in cinemas worldwide and will be available for free on the Guardian’s website from early December. Sign up to be the first to view it.
summary: The film NAZA features testimony from 24 Israeli officials involved in surveillance and remote killing of Palestinian civilians. NAZA is in cinemas worldwide and will screen for free on the Guardian’s website from early December.
author: Guardian World

title: Two Iranian-origin men found guilty of aiding Iran's plot to eliminate UK journalists
content:
Two men of Iranian origin, Mostafa Sepahvand, 41, and Farhad Javadi Manesh, 46, have been found guilty of assisting Tehran’s intelligence services in a plan to “eliminate” journalists based in the United Kingdom. The court heard they were hired through social media and tasked with surveillance and reconnaissance of potential targets.

According to the judgment, Sepahvand and Javadi Manesh conducted surveillance and reconnaissance between August 2024 and March of the previous year, aiming to facilitate violence against “subjects” in the UK. Their convictions relate specifically to these actions undertaken on behalf of the Iranian intelligence effort.
summary: Mostafa Sepahvand, 41, and Farhad Javadi Manesh, 46, were found guilty of assisting Tehran’s intelligence services in a plot to eliminate UK‑based journalists. They carried out surveillance and reconnaissance in the United Kingdom between August 2024 and March last year to prepare violence against the targets.
author: Guardian World

title: Andy Burnham says a win‑win EU deal could be done, likening it to 2016 Brexit expectations
content: Prime minister says reset could be a deal ‘like the Brexit people thought they were voting for in 2016’ Andy Burnham has said he believes a “win-win” deal could be done with the EU that could be “more like the Brexit that people thought they were voting for in 2016”. The prime minister was meeting fellow leaders at the European Political Community summit in Dublin, ahead of a keenly anticipated EU-UK summit next week, where he hopes to bring Britain closer to Europe.
summary: Andy Burnham said a “win‑win” deal with the EU could be done and would be “more like the Brexit that people thought they were voting for in 2016”. The prime minister met fellow leaders at the European Political Community summit in Dublin ahead of an EU‑UK summit the following week.
author: Guardian World

title: Microsoft starts restoring services after global Outlook and Teams outage
content:
Microsoft has started restoring services as it works to end a global outage that disrupted its Microsoft 365 suite. The company said a portion of servers are back online and a streamlined recovery process is under way after nearly 130,000 users worldwide reported access problems with Outlook, Teams and other applications.

Down Detector recorded a spike in reports, showing almost 130,000 incidents affecting Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams, SharePoint, OneDrive and the AI assistant Copilot. Microsoft indicated that the recovery effort aims to fully restore these services.
summary: Microsoft said a portion of servers are returning to service and a streamlined recovery process is under way following a global outage that affected its Microsoft 365 suite. Nearly 130,000 users worldwide reported access issues with Outlook, Teams, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, SharePoint, OneDrive and Copilot.
author: Guardian World

title: Pat Cummins defends Cricket Australia’s handling of 2018 sandpaper scandal
content: Cummins speaks about allegations in Usman Khawaja’s book about the 2018 ball-tampering incident Cummins says there’s a ‘proper way to do things’ Cummins says he believes there was a proper way to handle the sandpaper incident, pointing to the Cricket Australia investigation shortly afterwards. There’s a very proper way to do things and improve. I think that investigation was a proper way to do it. Everyone was asked in the circumstances about a game very quickly after. So that’s for CA. I think you can maybe argue whether the judgements were fair, but what can you do? I got asked all the questions, answered them all fairly. That’s my story, so I think he’s wrong. The details really matter in that difference. So perhaps there was conversations with Cameron Bancroft around taking sandpaper out and how to do it. That doesn’t mean that everyone in that dressing room knew what was going on.
summary: Cummins speaks about allegations in Usman Khawaja’s book about the 2018 ball-tampering incident Cummins says there’s a ‘proper way to do things’ Cummins says he believes there was a proper way to handle the sandpaper incident, pointing to the Cricket Australia investigation shortly afterwards. There’s a very proper way to do things and improve.
author: Guardian World

title: China declines to host UN COP33 climate summit in 2028
content:
China has ruled out hosting the Cop33 UN climate summit in 2028 after months of deliberations, according to the Guardian. The decision leaves the field open for other Asian countries to hold the summit.  

The move disappoints many countries and climate experts who had hoped the world’s biggest emitter would take the global lead on the climate crisis, noting that the United States under Donald Trump has vacated all forms of international climate cooperation.
summary: China has ruled out hosting the UN COP33 climate summit in 2028, leaving the field open for other Asian countries. The decision disappointed many countries and climate experts who had hoped the world’s biggest emitter would lead, as the US under Donald Trump has vacated all forms of international climate cooperation.
author: Guardian World

title: Blade Runner 2099 final trailer reveals plot for Nov. 25 Prime Video release
content: One of the most anticipated fall TV series, " Blade Runner 2099, " recently dropped its final neon-tinted trailer, and now we’ve finally got a handle on the plot dynamics of this dystopian thriller set in the cyberpunk world of Ridley Scott's original. Prime Video's bold and brooding 8-episode series lands Nov. 25 as a tangential sequel to Denis Villeneuve's "Blade Runner 2049," unfolding some 50 years after the 2017 feature film. Now the artificial inmates are running the asylum when violent replicant uprisings flip the script, causing humanity to become second-class citizens. "In Los Angeles 2099, Cora (Hunter Schafer) lived her entire life on the run, a chameleon forced to adopt numerous identities," states Prime Video's synopsis. "To secure a stable future for her brother, she assumes one final identity and is forced to partner with Olwen (Michelle Yeoh), a Blade Runner who’s confronting the end of her life. The two are pulled into a widening conspiracy that poses an existential threat to a city that’s fighting to be reborn." This engrossing final trailer reveals more of the detailed noir world and Cora's plight to blend into society as a Blade Runner who links up with Olwen, an aging replicant exterminator, for an uneasy partnership. Here, a tense scene plays out in this preview as Cora undergoes an intense police station screening while being used as a resistance pawn to help take back the city from usurping androids. But another deep mystery lies hidden in plain sight! "You have to see the lie that is in front of you," warns Yeoh's dying synthetic cop. Will "Blade Runner 2099" usher in a new era for the sci-fi franchise? (Image credit: Prime Video) " Blade Runner 2099 " sports a spirited cast that includes Dimitri Abold ("The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes") and Lewis Gribben ("Somewhere Boy”) in collaboration with Katelyn Rose Downey ("The Nun II"), Daniel Rigby ('Renegade Nell"), Johnny Harris ("A Gentleman in Moscow"), Amy Lennox ("Only Child"), Sheila Atim ("The Woman King") and Matthew Needham ("House of the Dragon”). Delivered by creator and showrunner Silka Louisa ("Shining Girls"), and executive produced by Silka Louisa and Ridley Scott’s Scott Free Productions, "Blade Runner 2099" lands on Prime Video beginning Nov. 25, 2026.

title: Pakistani astronaut to be first international visitor to China's Tiangong on Shenzhou 24
content: An astronaut from Pakistan is set to launch on China's Shenzhou 24 mission in the coming weeks and become the first-ever international visitor to the Tiangong space station. A pair of astronaut candidates from Pakistan have been training at the Astronaut Centre of China in Beijing, following an agreement reached between China and Pakistan in Islamabad in February 2025 and a subsequent selection process. China's human spaceflight agency confirmed in a Nov. 7 press statement that the upcoming Shenzhou 24 mission will carry one of the astronauts. The agency also released a mission patch. "China and Pakistan are all-weather strategic cooperative partners," Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said Nov. 9. "Having the Pakistani astronaut on board China's spaceships will mark the first-ever joint mission of Chinese and foreign astronauts in the history of China's manned space program." It is not yet known which of the two candidates will fly on Shenzhou 24. They were named in Pakistani press reports as Muhammad Zeeshan Ali and Khurram Daud, both pilots from the country's military forces. The pair were chosen from a wider pool of around 20 finalists. The chosen candidate will fly as a payload specialist on Shenzhou 24 along with two Chinese colleagues, while the other will be on standby as a backup. While the Chinese astronauts will be starting a six-month-long stay in space, the Pakistani astronaut will spend roughly a week in orbit aboard Tiangong during a standard crew rotation period. He will then return to Earth aboard the departing Shenzhou 23 spacecraft, along with two Chinese astronauts who will have completed a six-month-long stay in orbit. The arrangement means changes to China's usual "three in, three out" Tiangong crew rotations. One of the three Shenzhou 23 astronauts, who arrived at Tiangong on May 24, will stay aboard and complete China's first-ever year-long stay in orbit, while the Pakistani astronaut will take their seat aboard Shenzhou 23 to return home. During his stay in space, the Pakistani astronaut will be responsible for four research payloads selected from more than 300 proposals, according to Pakistan's space agency, SUPARCO. China has not announced a timeline for the launch of the Shenzhou 24 mission, but it is expected to lift off before the end of November. The Shenzhou 23 astronauts currently aboard Tiangong are closing in on 180 days in orbit, nearing an end to their six months in space. Shenzhou 24 will launch from Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in the Gobi Desert on a Long March 2F rocket. The identities of the crew for China's human spaceflight missions are typically closely guarded, and will only be revealed in a press conference a day ahead of launch. Shenzhou 24's Long March 2F rocket will be rolled out to the pad around a week ahead of launch. The partnership between the two countries has already produced Chinese-launched Pakistani satellites, including a lunar cubesat, and a Pakistani-built rover due to fly on the Chang'e-8 lunar landing mission.
summary: A Pakistani astronaut will launch on China's Shenzhou 24 mission in the coming weeks, becoming the first international visitor to the Tiangong space station. The selected pilot, named Muhammad Zeeshan Ali or Khurram Daud, will serve as a payload specialist for roughly a week before returning to Earth aboard the departing Shenzhou 23 spacecraft.

title: Euclid telescope releases first major data on dark matter and energy
content: On Thursday (Nov. 12), the Euclid space telescope released its first major batch of data, capturing the light of more than a billion objects over an area of sky as big as 9,500 full moons. The data release lays the foundation for one of the largest-ever 3D maps of the cosmos and many groundbreaking discoveries about the nature of dark energy and dark matter. The European Space Agency 's (ESA) Euclid space telescope has been called the "Dark Universe Detective" because of its capability to investigate the dual mysteries of dark matter, the universe's most mysterious stuff, and dark energy, the force accelerating the expansion of the universe. Collectively, these cosmic elements are sometimes referred to as the dark universe. The new data release, designated DR1-Foundation, was built from 13 months of observations and is accompanied by a multitude of images, including large sky mosaics. It marks the first major release of mission data since Euclid launched in mid-2023. The core of the Messier 81 galaxy group as seen by Euclid. (Image credit: ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA, image processing by J.-C. Cuillandre and E. Bertin) "These are far more than beautiful pictures; today marks a scientific milestone in our study of the cosmos," ESA's Director of Science, Carole Mundell said in a statement. "This major Euclid data release represents the largest space-based survey of its kind, laying the foundation of future discovery in a new regime for astronomy and demonstrating the excellence of European technology, science and international collaboration." What's in the Euclid release The ESA put into raw numbers the sheer number of celestial objects viewed by the Dark Universe Detective and contained in DR1-Foundation. That includes light spectra from 160 million sources, over 900 million galaxies, and 60 million candidates for quasars, regions of space dominated by feeding supermassive black holes. "This is a change in scale from Euclid's previous releases, which included a few days of observations over around 60 degrees squared of sky," ESA's Euclid project scientist Valeria Pettorino said. "We're now releasing more than a year of data covering a significantly larger area. This unlocks groundbreaking science." NGC 1291, a striking ring galaxy lying around 33 million light-years away from us, as seen by Euclid. (Image credit: ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA, image processing by J.-C. Cuillandre and E. Bertin) Euclid can see such a vast number of cosmic objects thanks to the fact that its space-based position helps it avoid interference caused by Earth's atmosphere. This includes clusters of galaxies and even larger superclusters. The study of these objects, some of the largest structures in the cosmos, can reveal how matter came together across the larger network of gas, dust and dark matter called the cosmic web. "Euclid doesn't just look far back in time — it does so across huge areas of sky," Euclid Consortium member Barbara Sartoris of JL Lagrange Laboratory, Nice, France, explained. "This gives us an unprecedented view of large samples of ancient galaxy clusters that were previously out of reach. "We will explore these in the coming months to learn how these giants grew, and decipher what they reveal about the dark universe." The Horologium supercluster of galaxies as seen by Euclid. (Image credit: ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA, image processing by J.-C. Cuillandre and E. Bertin) Another exciting element of the new Euclid data release is the 15,000 strong gravitational lensing candidates catalogued by the space telescope. Gravitational lensing is an element of the universe first explained in Einstein magnum opus, general relativity, in 1915. General relativity says that objects with mass cause the very fabric of space to warp, and that gravity arises from this warping. But there is another consequence. When light passes this curvature, its usually straight path is curved. That means when light from a single background source passes an object with great mass, like a galaxy or galaxy cluster, a strong gravitational lens, it can arrive at our telescopes at different times. As a result of this strong lensing, background sources can be greatly amplified. It is an effect that the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) has been using to great effect to study galaxies in the early universe. Gravitational lenses observed by the Euclid telescope. (Image credit: ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA, image processing by N. Lines and T. Li) Thus, the prospect of mapping 15,000 strong gravitational lenses is monumental, especially in studying the rate at which the universe is expanding and thus the effect of dark energy. "Strong lensing provides unique insight into the dark universe, allowing us to 'weigh' individual galaxies, including their invisible dark matter, and explore how the universe is expanding," Natalie Lines of the University of Portsmouth, U. K., and member of the Euclid Consortium, said. "Over 10 years ago, we forecast that Euclid would revolutionize the field of strong lens discovery. That day is finally here." The best is yet to come Arguably, the most exciting thing about DR1-Foundation is that Euclid is just getting started. The area of sky covered from spring 2024 to spring 2025 represents just 14% of Euclid's target for its entire six-year survey. That means whatever scientists discover from this data release could be the tip of the iceberg in terms of how the Dark Universe Detective will change our understanding of the cosmos. The area of sky covered from spring 2024 to spring 2025, just 14% of the mission’s target for the entire six-year survey. (Image credit: ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA; ESA/Gaia/DPAC; ESA/Planck Collaboration) "DR1-Foundation includes raw data, calibrated images, catalogues, and spectra over a huge sky area, with enough statistics touncover even rare objects," Valeria said. "It will be used to map the large-scale structure of the universe in unprecedented detail. "So much discovery is yet to come."
summary: The European Space Agency's Euclid telescope released its first major data batch, capturing light from over a billion objects to begin mapping the cosmos. This release includes 15,000 gravitational lensing candidates and covers 14% of the telescope's six-year survey target.

title: Judy Collins Recalls Joni Mitchell Singing 'Both Sides, Now' Over Phone
content: As she continues her farewell tour, the US singer-songwriter answers your questions on romance with Stephen Stills, friendship with Carly Simon and how folk underpins all pop How did you come into Joni Mitchell ’s orbit and how did you end up recording Both Sides, Now before she did? Steve-bayley I’m 48 years sober, but in the old days I drank. One night in 1967, I was passed out and the phone rang at about 3am. It was my friend [the musician, songwriter and producer] Al Kooper. He said he’d been at a club and had run into this woman, Joni, who wrote songs. He put her on the phone and she sang Both Sides, Now over the phone. It was brilliant. I said: “I’ll be right over.” I recorded it the next day and it became a huge hit. I don’t think Joni was too happy that I was the first to record it, but she was very generous and I’ve since recorded many of her songs. She was unknown then, so I’m proud that I was able to help introduce her to the world. She’s one of the great writers of all time.
summary: Folk singer Judy Collins explained that she recorded "Both Sides, Now" after Joni Mitchell sang the song to her over the phone in 1967. Collins stated that the track became a major hit and she is proud to have helped introduce Mitchell to the world.

title: Review: Johnny Depp stars in faithful A Christmas Carol adaptation
content:
A new film adaptation of Charles Dickens’s A Christmas Carol has been released, starring Johnny Depp as the titular character. The movie, directed by Ti West and written by Nathaniel Halpern, is described as a faithful and serviceable adaptation that adheres to the traditional narrative beats and familiar episodes of the classic story. Depp appears in the film wearing a top hat and heavy makeup, portraying the miser before his redemption.

The review characterizes the film as decent and unexpectedly watchable, noting that it explores whether a man can earn redemption before it is too late. While the adaptation sticks closely to the original plot involving three Christmas ghosts, it includes a few twists. The source suggests that Depp is particularly effective in his portrayal of the legendary miser prior to his transformation.
summary: The new film adaptation of Dickens's A Christmas Carol stars Johnny Depp as the titular miser. Screenwriter Nathaniel Halpern and director Ti West created a serviceable version that follows the original narrative with a few twists.

title: England’s wheelchair rugby league squad aim to retain World Cup title against France
content:
England’s wheelchair rugby league squad enters Friday’s World Cup final against France with the goal of retaining the title they won in 2022. Beyond the objective of securing another trophy, the team aims to inspire greater participation in their fast-growing and compelling sport. The upcoming match serves as a significant moment for the discipline, which is part of the broader landscape of British sport often evaluated by metrics such as attendances, viewing figures, and revenue.

Lewis King, the captain of the England wheelchair rugby league team, shares his personal journey to highlight the sport’s impact. In 2009, at the age of 24, King was left partially paralysed following a blood clot on his spine that necessitated an emergency operation. At that time, he felt that playing sport was impossible. His experience underscores the transformative potential of wheelchair rugby league for athletes facing similar physical challenges.
summary: England’s wheelchair rugby league team will face France in the World Cup final, hoping to retain the trophy they won in 2022. Captain Lewis King, who became partially paralysed in 2009 after a blood clot on his spine, recalls how difficult it was to play sport before his emergency operation.

title: Lewis Hamilton calls Israel's Gaza actions appalling after Rafah visit
content:
Formula One driver Lewis Hamilton stated on Wednesday that Israel must permit aid trucks into Gaza, describing the situation as an “appalling” genocide. This statement came one day after his visit to the Rafah border crossing in Egypt. Hamilton, a seven-time world champion, arrived in El Arish on Tuesday to observe the logistics of humanitarian support.

During his trip, Hamilton toured the Rafah crossing and the Egyptian Red Crescent’s aid warehouses. He was briefed by aid workers on how supplies are prepared and coordinated before being sent into Gaza.
summary: Lewis Hamilton stated that Israel must allow aid trucks into Gaza following his visit to the Rafah border crossing in Egypt. The Formula One driver toured aid warehouses and was briefed on how assistance is prepared and coordinated for delivery.

title: France face South Africa amid injury crisis and poor head-to-head record
content:
France will face South Africa at the Stade de France this Friday night, a matchup described as a likely meeting of the two best teams in the inaugural Nations Championship. Although the tournament final is scheduled for two weeks later at Twickenham, the immediate fixture pits back-to-back Six Nations champions France against back-to-back world champions South Africa. This contest is viewed as a critical hurdle for the French team in the year leading up to the Springboks' potential bid for a third consecutive World Cup title.

The rivalry remains heavily skewed in favor of the Springboks, who have won nine of the last ten meetings between the two sides over the past 15 years. South Africa has also secured the last five encounters held in Paris. While other European teams, including England, Ireland, and Wales, hold better head-to-head records against the Springboks during this period, France’s sole victory occurred in Marseille in 2022. That success was followed by a quarter-final exit for the French from their home World Cup the next year, a result attributed by head coach Fabien Galthié to a current injury crisis that complicates his squad’s efforts to overcome the South African defense.
summary: France are facing an injury crisis ahead of their match against South Africa, a team they have beaten only once in their last ten meetings. The article notes that France have lost their last five home games against the Springboks, including a World Cup quarter-final defeat.

title: Crystal Palace dismisses Pierre Sage after 16 games, Thomas Frank in advanced talks
content:
Crystal Palace have dismissed manager Pierre Sage after 16 games, a decision that has cost the club more than £10 million. Sage, who was appointed in mid‑June on a three‑year contract to replace Oliver Glasner, saw the team fall to the bottom of the Premier League following a 3‑1 defeat by Liverpool on Sunday. The club has suggested that Sage could return to Lens after his departure.

The club is in advanced talks with Thomas Frank to take over the managerial role. Frank was dismissed by Tottenham Hotspur in February and has been without a club since. He is regarded as the leading candidate to replace Sage, having spoken to Palace during the summer and expressing a desire for a new challenge after a successful spell at Brentford.

Palace hope Frank will assume the position before the next Saturday’s trip to Coventry, providing a swift transition in the club’s leadership.
summary: Pierre Sage was sacked as Crystal Palace manager after 16 games, following a 3-1 defeat by Liverpool that left the club bottom of the Premier League. Thomas Frank, dismissed by Spurs in February, is in advanced talks to become the next manager, with hopes he will take charge before the Saturday trip to Coventry.

title: Michael Carrick was just the latest fall guy for Manchester United’s dysfunctional hierarchy | Jamie Jackson
content:
Michael Carrick’s recent sacking highlights the ongoing dysfunction at Manchester United, a club plagued by disastrous decisions and confused appointments since Sir Alex Ferguson’s retirement in 2013. The instability is exemplified by the chaotic process surrounding Carrick’s successor, where Eddie Howe was initially a favorite to take over the role. Howe had been selected by Jason Wilcox, United’s current director of football, and was also the preferred candidate of Dan Ashworth, Wilcox’s predecessor, to replace Erik ten Hag following the Dutchman’s dismissal in October 2024.

However, the appointment process devolved into conflict, with Wilcox disagreeing with Ashworth’s preference. Ultimately, Sir Jim Ratcliffe sided with Wilcox, appointing Ruben Amorim instead. This decision contributed to Ashworth’s departure just five months after joining the club, underscoring the alarming lack of cohesion within the hierarchy that Carrick was unable to manage.
summary: Michael Carrick was just the latest fall guy for Manchester United’s dysfunctional hierarchy | Jamie Jackson.

title: Indigenous activist Rikki Dank urges Albanese to block new fossil fuels
content:
Indigenous climate activist Rikki Dank, a Gudanji and Wakaya traditional owner, joined Greta Thunberg at the Cop summit to urge Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese to halt new coal, oil, and gas production. Dank, who is currently taking the Australian government to the UN human rights committee regarding its coal and gas exports, addressed a media crowd while draped in traditional dress.

Dank delivered an impassioned plea for Albanese to “stop speaking and start listening” to the Australian people. She explicitly called on the Prime Minister to heed the public’s demand for no more new fossil fuel projects, emphasizing the need for immediate action on climate change.
summary: Indigenous climate activist Rikki Dank stood alongside Greta Thunberg at the Cop summit to demand that Anthony Albanese stop new coal, oil, and gas. title: John Kerry calls Trump biggest loser for scrapping climate action at Cop31
content:
Former US Secretary of State John Kerry described Donald Trump as the “biggest loser we’ve seen in a long time” for abandoning climate action and ceding clean-energy dominance to China. Speaking at the Cop31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, Kerry criticized the president for withdrawing the United States from the international climate process and eliminating measures designed to reduce planet-heating emissions.

The Trump administration has not sent a delegation to the annual UN climate talks, which began on Monday. Kerry noted that the climate crisis remains a significant issue for voters, highlighting the contrast between the US withdrawal and the participation of nearly all other nations at the summit.
summary: Former US secretary of state John Kerry criticized Donald Trump for withdrawing the US from international climate processes and ceding clean-energy dominance to China. Kerry made these remarks at the Cop31 climate summit in Turkey, where the Trump administration sent no delegation.

content:
US existing home sales reached a 16-year low in October, with sales of already built units falling to 3.75 million. The National Association of Realtors reported that this volume represented an 8.8% decrease from the previous year. According to the data released on Wednesday, buyers were driven away by record-high mortgage rates, which had reached nearly a three-year high, alongside rising inflation.

The median existing-home sales price increased slightly to $416,700. While the north-east region saw sales hold steady, declines were recorded in the midwest, south, and west.

title: College students rally on 40+ campuses to support Starbucks baristas boycott
content:
On Thursday, students, elected officials and allies held rallies at more than 40 U.S. college campuses to support the Starbucks Workers United boycott campaign. The rallies come as the union approaches five years of stalled negotiations with Starbucks over contract terms.

Starbucks Workers United is demanding higher pay and stronger staffing standards, including a $17‑an‑hour minimum wage for baristas and a minimum of three workers per store. The union has urged the public to boycott Starbucks until a new contract is reached.
summary: College students rally on 40+ campuses to support Starbucks baristas boycott.
author: Guardian Business

title: Nvidia’s Jensen Huang to testify to US Congress amid scandal, reports say, as CFO Colette Kress replaces him as interim CEO – follow live
content: Nvidia’s value slumps by $888bn this week as scandal over longtime CEO’s two affairs, including with a suspected Chinese spy, engulfs chip maker Analysis: Jensen Huang built an AI kingdom. What now? Full report: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO Too big – and too well-connected – to sack? Huang does not enjoy the supercharged voting rights that are par for the course elsewhere – his shareholding is a plain vanilla 3.6%. On the other hand, Nvidia’s board does not appear to have spent much time worrying about succession planning and “key person risk” or other standard concerns of corporate governance wonks outside the US.
summary: Nvidia’s value slumps by $888bn this week as scandal over longtime CEO’s two affairs, including with a suspected Chinese spy, engulfs chip maker Analysis: Jensen Huang built an AI kingdom. What now?
author: Guardian Business

title: Liquid-phase growth strategy densifies ceramic films at low temperature
content:
Ceramic films are essential components in solid‑state batteries, energy‑conversion devices, and electronic systems. Their production typically relies on high‑temperature sintering, a process that can trigger elemental volatilization, compositional segregation, and unwanted interfacial reactions.  

Consequently, creating dense, compositionally uniform ceramic films at lower temperatures remains a significant challenge for researchers and manufacturers.
summary: Ceramic films used in solid‑state batteries, energy conversion devices, and electronic systems typically require high‑temperature sintering, which can cause elemental volatilization, compositional segregation, and undesirable interfacial reactions. A liquid‑phase growth strategy aims to densify these films at lower temperatures, addressing the challenge of achieving dense, compositionally uniform ceramic films.
author: Phys.org

title: Lemon waste yields more flexible bioplastic than commercial counterpart, study finds
content: A study published in Polymers details the conversion of lemon processing residues into biopolymers. The research, authored by CETEC’s ANIPH coordinator and partners from the Viss and PHAntastic projects, utilized lemon industry byproducts as carbon sources. The team employed the halophilic archaeon Haloferax mediterranei to produce PHBV from these waste materials.
summary: Lemon waste yields more flexible bioplastic than commercial counterpart, study finds.
author: Phys.org

title: Skin microbes give largetooth sawfish an invisible force field, study finds
content:
New research from Flinders University has found that the large freshwater sawfish, the critically endangered largetooth sawfish (Pristis pristis), may rely on microscopic communities that live on its skin to survive tough environmental conditions. The study suggests that these tiny microbes could provide a kind of invisible force field for the fish’s young during dry‑season periods when oxygen levels drop.

By highlighting the role of skin microbes in helping the species endure challenging dry‑season conditions, the research offers a fresh perspective on conservation strategies for the largetooth sawfish.
summary: New research led by Flinders University shows microscopic communities on the skin of the critically endangered largetooth sawfish (Pristis pristis) may help the animals survive dry‑season conditions. The microbes could provide an invisible force field for the sawfish's young when environmental conditions get tough.
author: Phys.org

title: Roman timber fort found in Preseli hills sparks renewed interest in Welsh mythic emperor
content: A recent discovery of a Roman timber fort in the Preseli hills of Pembrokeshire, southwest Wales, has brought a medieval Welsh legend into fresh focus. The find highlights the region’s historical significance and renews interest in the legend associated with the site.
summary: The recent discovery of a Roman timber fort in the Preseli hills of Pembrokeshire, southwest Wales, has brought a medieval Welsh legend into fresh focus. The find has reignited interest in the emperor immortalized in Welsh mythology.
author: Phys.org

title: Dead star spins every 8 minutes, paired with sun‑like star, emits radio pulses
content: Scientists at Curtin University’s node at the International Center for Radio Astronomy Research (ICRAR) have traced mysterious radio pulses to an unusual stellar pair. The system consists of a dead star that spins every eight minutes and a companion star similar to the Sun. The link between the rapid rotation and the radio emissions was established by the Curtin research team.
summary: Scientists at the Curtin University node at ICRAR linked mysterious radio pulses to a pairing of a dead star that spins every eight minutes and a sun‑like star. The system emits radio signals every eight minutes.
author: Phys.org

title: Study finds earnings call Q&A still provides useful info beyond written reports
content: Specialized language used by analysts and management during listed companies’ Q&A sessions can be difficult for individual investors to understand. Nevertheless, Kaisa Penttinen’s doctoral dissertation in accounting at the University of Vaasa, Finland, demonstrates that these sessions still provide useful information beyond what is disclosed in written reports alone.
summary: The specialized language used by analysts and management in listed companies' Q&A sessions can be challenging for individual investors to follow. Kaisa Penttinen's doctoral dissertation in accounting at the University of Vaasa, Finland, shows these sessions still deliver useful information beyond what is disclosed in written reports alone.
author: Phys.org

title: Kuiper belt beyond Neptune contains icy bodies with frozen water, methane, ammonia
content: Space dust particles have been found that point to an ancient reservoir of heavy‑oxygen water in the Kuiper belt. The Kuiper belt, located beyond Neptune, is a ring of icy bodies that have escaped much of the processing experienced by objects closer to the Sun. Unlike the rocky and metallic asteroid belt, Kuiper belt objects are composed mainly of frozen water, methane and ammonia, mixed with rock and dust.
summary: The Kuiper belt lies beyond Neptune and contains icy bodies that have avoided much solar processing. These objects are made mostly of frozen water, methane, ammonia, rock, and dust.
author: Phys.org

title: UK military partners with civilian astronomers to monitor foreign spy satellites
content: The UK military says it cannot match the advanced surveillance and counter‑surveillance programmes operated by the United States, China and Russia. To address this gap, it is collaborating with civilian astronomers to develop a method for monitoring foreign spy satellites using ground‑based telescopes.
summary: The UK cannot match the advanced surveillance and counter‑surveillance programmes of the US, China and Russia. It is collaborating with civilian astronomers to develop a method for monitoring spy satellites using ground‑based telescopes.
author: New Scientist

title: Euclid telescope releases 900 million galaxy images covering 367 square degrees
content:
The European Space Agency has released a new set of observations from the Euclid space telescope, titled DR1-Foundation. Launched in 2023, the telescope is on a six-year mission to image about one-third of the sky to create the most detailed 3D map of the cosmos. The latest data covers an area equivalent to 9,500 full moons and includes 900 million galaxies. A specific mosaic of 740 images, collected in autumn 2024 and spring 2025, spans 367 square degrees of the northern sky and totals 500 gigapixels at full resolution.

The release features high-resolution views of several celestial objects, including the spiral galaxy Messier 81, located approximately 12 million light-years from Earth. Detailed imagery of Messier 81 reveals its disc, where individual stars are visible, as well as nearby structures such as the smaller galaxy NGC 3077 and foreground galactic cirrus from the Milky Way. The data also showcases NGC 1291, a hazy galaxy about 33 million light-years away, where active star formation is visible as small blue-hued dots against a background of more distant galaxies.

Additionally, the observations include Abell 3128, a cluster of hundreds of galaxies situated around 800 million light-years away. This cluster contains a diverse array of galaxies, including spirals and ellipticals. The image of Abell 3128 also captures a strong gravitational lens in the center, where light from a more distant galaxy has been warped by a massive foreground object.
summary: Euclid telescope releases 900 million galaxy images covering 367 square degrees.
author: New Scientist

title: Nvidia Faces Espionage Scandal That Threatens Global AI Chip Markets
content: Columnist Jacob Aron examines how Nvidia became the central pillar of the AI industry. The article notes that an espionage scandal involving the world’s largest company threatens to destabilize economies that depend on its AI chips.
summary: An espionage scandal has hit Nvidia, the biggest company in the world. The fallout could destabilise economies that rely on its AI chips, according to columnist Jacob Aron, who explains Nvidia's role as the AI industry's lynchpin.
author: New Scientist

title: Pink noise during sleep may improve memory in Alzheimer's patients
content: Emerging evidence suggests that pink noise signals may enhance the brain’s capacity to remove waste products. New indications point to the potential for this acoustic stimulation to improve memory performance in individuals suffering from Alzheimer’s disease.
summary: Pink noise signals may help the brain clear waste products. Early indications suggest this could improve memory performance in people with Alzheimer's.
author: New Scientist

title: Euclid Reveals 900 Million Galaxies and 15,000 Gravitational Lensing Candidates
content: Unprecedented view of cosmos provided by Euclid mission throws up many more cases of gravitational lensing A mission to create the largest ever 3D map of the universe has revealed more than 900m galaxies in its first major data release together with about 15,000 potential cases of a phenomenon that could help unlock the secrets of the “dark universe”. Launched in July 2023, the European Space Agency’s Euclid mission promised to create the largest cosmic map ever made, encompassing a third of the sky and more than 10bn years of cosmic history.
summary: The Euclid mission released its first major data set, identifying more than 900 million galaxies and about 15,000 potential gravitational lensing cases. These findings could help unlock the secrets of the dark universe.
author: Guardian Science

title: NASA Ames Stars of the Month: November 2026
content:
NASA Ames Science Directorate has announced its Stars of the Month for November 2026, recognizing the contributions of Alyssa Villanueva, Steve Howell, and Samuel LeBlanc. The directorate stated that these individuals exemplify the entrepreneurial spirit, technical expertise, and collaborative disposition required to explore the world and beyond.

Alyssa Villanueva, an engineer at Blue Marble within the Space Biosciences Division, received the Space Biosciences Star. She is a member of the LEIA (Lunar Explorer Instrument for space biology Applications) team and was recognized for her technical excellence, dedication, and support to her colleagues. Her work has been essential to the team’s test efforts, particularly in the preparation and execution of engineering validation testing.

Steve Howell was named the Astrophysics Star for his leadership of scientific teams on numerous international space missions. His pioneering work in astronomical instrumentation has advanced both space- and ground-based telescope imaging. Additionally, the Astronomical Society of the Pacific recently awarded him the Catherine Wolfe Bruce Gold Medal in recognition of his lifetime of major contributions to the field.

Samuel LeBlanc, a research scientist for the Bay Area Environmental Research Institute in the Earth Science Division, received the Earth Science Star. He was recognized for exceptional technical leadership and innovative thinking in advancing Ames’ flight planning capabilities for NASA airborne science missions. His contributions have positioned Ames at the forefront of airborne science flight planning, enabling successful and cost-effective missions that maximize scientific returns both within and outside the Agency.
summary: NASA Ames Stars of the Month: November 2026.
author: NASA News

title: Kapso Open‑Source Engine Enables Iterative Learning from Enterprise Data
content:
Alireza and Majid, founders of Leeroo, have open-sourced Kapso, an engine designed for iterative learning from enterprise data. The team, which previously built AI systems for products at LinkedIn and Meta, states that Kapso is intended to automate the bottom-up process of investigating, forming hypotheses, and experimenting within large, messy data environments. They argue that traditional approaches, such as consultants gathering context in meetings or teams defining business ontologies upfront, are often too slow for execution in complex settings.

Kapso operates by accepting an objective and success criteria, then working toward an optimum solution that can be deployed on a user’s stack. The system utilizes a bank of lessons induced or deduced from past experiments, where each lesson carries a credence score, applicable conditions, and supporting evidence. An ideation module proposes new ideas based on these lessons, re-ranks them by expected return against budget, and sends the top candidates to an implementor. A separate verifier module, which no experiment can access or cheat, validates the results of each run.

The architecture allows for the evolution of success criteria and evaluation tests, with experimentation modules proposing updates that the verifier can approve or reject. After each run, a `learn()` function updates the lesson bank’s scores and boundaries using the new evidence. The system supports A/B testing of bank changes by running identical builds with previous and updated banks. Built on git, the bank allows users to share, list, and update experiences via CLI commands. Kapso is described as model-agnostic and coding-agent-agnostic, with a deployment workflow that adapts solutions to target stacks such as Docker, Modal, BentoCloud, and LangGraph.

The developers report that Kapso achieved top results on several public benchmarks and live competitions. In predictive modeling on relational databases, it ranked first on RelBench, a benchmark by Kumo AI (now Nvidia) and Stanford, ahead of the best tabular foundation model. In ML engineering, it placed first on OpenAI's MLE-bench at submission and remains among the top open-source systems. In AI competitions, it outperformed the best agent reported by Sakana AI for ALE-Bench and ran autonomously at the live International Olympiad in AI 2026, finishing above all 471 human contestants and within the top three AI systems.

Leeroo also maintains a public bank for ML and Data at Leeroopedia, which contains approximately 100,000 pages extracted from experimenting on papers and repositories. The platform handles about six million requests per month, with roughly 28% of traffic coming from AI agents. The founders are currently seeking to assist growing companies with complex data estates across multiple systems and functions, particularly those with stretched data and AI teams.
summary: Alireza and Majid of Leeroo have open‑sourced Kapso, an AI‑native engine that runs experiments, deploys the best solution, and learns from each run on enterprise data. Kapso uses a bank of lessons with credence scores, verifies results, and adapts solutions to target stacks such as Docker, Modal, and BentoCloud.
